texts.heb.11.28: Pela fé celebrou a paschoa e o derramamento de sangue, para que o destruidor dos primogenitos os não tocasse.
texts.heb.11.29: Pela fé passaram o Mar Vermelho, como por terra secca; o que intentando os egypcios, se afogaram.
texts.heb.11.30: Pela fé cairam os muros de Jericó, sendo sitiados durante sete dias.
texts.heb.11.31: Pela fé Rahab, a meretriz, não pereceu com os incredulos, acolhendo em paz os espias.
texts.heb.11.32: E que mais direi? Faltar-me-hia o tempo, contando de Gideon, e de Barac, e de Sansão, e de Jefthe, e de David, e de Samuel e dos prophetas:
texts.heb.11.33: Os quaes pela fé venceram reinos, exercitaram justiça, alcançaram promessas, fecharam as boccas dos leões,
texts.heb.11.34: Apagaram a força do fogo, escaparam do fio da espada, da fraqueza tiraram forças, na batalha se esforçaram, pozeram em fugida os exercitos dos estranhos.
texts.heb.11.35: As mulheres tornaram a receber pela resurreição os seus mortos, e outros foram estirados, não acceitando o seu livramento, para alcançarem uma melhor resurreição.
texts.heb.11.36: E outros experimentaram escarneos e açoites, e até cadeias e prisões;
texts.heb.11.37: Foram apedrejados, serrados, tentados, mortos ao fio da espada; andaram vestidos de pelles de ovelhas e de cabras, desamparados, afflictos e maltratados
texts.heb.11.38: (Dos quaes o mundo não era digno), errantes pelos desertos, e montes, e covas e cavernas da terra.
texts.heb.11.39: E todos estes, tendo testemunho pela fé, não alcançaram a promessa:
texts.heb.11.40: Provendo Deus alguma coisa melhor a nosso respeito, para que sem nós não fossem aperfeiçoados.
texts.heb.12.1: Portanto nós tambem, pois que estamos rodeados de uma tão grande nuvem de testemunhas, deixemos toda a carga, e o peccado que tão commodamente nos rodeia, e corramos com paciencia a carreira que nos está proposta:
texts.heb.12.2: Olhando para Jesus, auctor e consummador da fé, o qual pelo gozo que lhe estava proposto supportou a cruz, desprezando a affronta, e assentou-se á dextra do throno de Deus.
texts.heb.12.3: Considerae pois aquelle que contra si mesmo supportou tal contradicção dos peccadores, para que não enfraqueçaes, desfallecendo em vossos animos.
texts.heb.12.4: Ainda não resististes até ao sangue, combatendo contra o peccado.
texts.heb.12.5: E já vos esquecestes da exhortação que, como a filhos, discorre comvosco: Filho meu, não desprezes a correcção do Senhor, e não desmaies quando por elle fores reprehendido;
texts.heb.12.6: Porque o Senhor corrige ao que ama, e açoita a qualquer que recebe por filho.
texts.heb.12.7: Se supportaes a correcção, Deus vos trata como a filhos; porque, que filho ha a quem o pae não corrija?
texts.heb.12.8: Mas, se estaes sem disciplina, da qual todos são feitos participantes, logo sois bastardos, e não filhos.
texts.heb.12.9: Tambem, na verdade, tivemos nossos paes, segundo a carne, para nos corrigir, e os reverenciámos: não nos sujeitaremos muito mais ao Pae dos espiritos, para vivermos?
texts.heb.12.10: Porque aquelles, na verdade, por um pouco de tempo, nos corrigiam como bem lhes parecia; porém este, para nosso proveito, para sermos participantes da sua sanctidade.
texts.heb.12.11: E, na verdade, toda a correcção, ao presente, não parece ser causa de gozo, senão de tristeza, mas depois produz um fructo pacifico de justiça aos exercitados por ella.
texts.heb.12.12: Portanto tornae a levantar as mãos cançadas, e os joelhos desconjuntados,
texts.heb.12.13: E fazei rectas veredas para os vossos pés, para que o que manqueja se não desvie inteiramente, antes seja sarado.
texts.heb.12.14: Segui a paz com todos, e a sanctificação, sem a qual ninguem verá o Senhor:
texts.heb.12.15: Attendendo a que ninguem se prive da graça de Deus, a que nenhuma raiz de amargura, brotando, vos perturbe, e por ella muitos se contaminem.
texts.heb.12.16: Que ninguem seja fornicario, ou profano, como Esaú, que por um manjar vendeu o seu direito de primogenitura.
texts.heb.12.17: Porque bem sabeis que, querendo ainda depois herdar a benção, foi rejeitado, porque não achou logar de arrependimento, ainda que com lagrimas o buscou.
texts.heb.12.18: Porque não chegastes ao monte que se não podia tocar, e ao fogo incendido, e á escuridão, e ás trevas, e á tempestade,
texts.heb.12.19: E ao sonido da trombeta, e á voz das palavras, a qual os que a ouviram pediram que se lhes não fallasse mais;
texts.heb.12.20: Porque não podiam supportar o que se lhes mandava: se até uma besta tocar o monte, será apedrejada ou passada com uma frecha.
texts.heb.12.21: E tão terrivel era a visão, que Moysés disse: Estou todo assombrado, e tremendo.
texts.heb.12.22: Mas chegastes ao monte de Sião, e á cidade do Deus vivo, á Jerusalem celestial, e aos muitos milhares de anjos;
texts.heb.12.23: Á assembléa geral e egreja dos primogenitos, que estão inscriptos nos céus, e a Deus, o juiz de todos, e aos espiritos dos justos aperfeiçoados;
texts.heb.12.24: E a Jesus, o Mediador do Novo Testamento, e ao sangue da aspersão, que falla melhores coisas do que o de Abel.
texts.heb.12.25: Vêde que não rejeiteis ao que falla; porque, se não escaparam aquelles que rejeitaram ao que na terra dava respostas divinas, muito menos escaparemos nós, se nos desviarmos d’aquelle que é dos céus:
texts.heb.12.26: A voz do qual moveu então a terra, porém agora annunciou, dizendo: Ainda uma vez commoverei, não só a terra, senão tambem o céu.
texts.heb.12.27: E esta palavra: Ainda uma vez, mostra a mudança das coisas moveis, como coisas feitas, para que as immoveis permaneçam.
texts.heb.12.28: Pelo que, recebendo o reino immovel, retenhamos a graça, pela qual sirvamos a Deus agradavelmente com reverencia e piedade;
texts.heb.12.29: Porque o nosso Deus é um fogo consumidor.
texts.heb.13.2: Não vos esqueçaes da hospitalidade, porque por ella alguns, não o sabendo, hospedaram anjos.
texts.heb.13.3: Lembrae-vos dos presos, como se juntamente estivesseis presos, e dos maltratados, como o sendo vós mesmos tambem no corpo.
texts.heb.13.4: Venerado seja entre todos o matrimonio e a cama sem macula; porém aos fornicadores e adulteros Deus os julgará.
texts.heb.13.5: Sejam os vossos costumes sem avareza, contentando-vos com o presente; porque elle disse: Não te deixarei, nem te desampararei.
texts.heb.13.6: De maneira que com confiança ousemos dizer: O Senhor é o meu ajudador, e não temerei o que o homem me possa fazer.
texts.heb.13.7: Lembrae-vos dos vossos pastores, que vos fallaram a palavra de Deus, a fé dos quaes imitae, attentando para a maneira da vida d’elles.
texts.heb.13.8: Jesus Christo é o mesmo hontem, e hoje, e eternamente.
texts.heb.13.9: Não vos deixeis levar ao redor por doutrinas varias e estranhas, porque bom é que o coração se fortifique com graça, e não com manjares, os quaes de nada aproveitaram aos que a elles se entregaram.
texts.heb.13.10: Temos um altar, do qual não tem poder de comer os que servem ao tabernaculo.
texts.heb.13.11: Porque os corpos dos animaes, cujo sangue é, pelo peccado, trazido pelo summo sacerdote para o sanctuario, são queimados fóra do arraial.
texts.heb.13.12: Portanto tambem Jesus, para sanctificar o povo pelo seu proprio sangue, padeceu fóra da porta.
texts.heb.13.13: Saiamos pois a elle fóra do arraial, levando o seu vituperio.
texts.heb.13.14: Porque não temos aqui cidade permanente, mas buscamos a futura.
texts.heb.13.15: Portanto offereçamos sempre por elle a Deus sacrificio de louvor, isto é, o fructo dos labios que confessam o seu nome.
texts.heb.13.16: E não vos esqueçaes da beneficencia e communicação, porque com taes sacrificios Deus se agrada.
texts.heb.13.17: Obedecei a vossos pastores, e sujeitae-vos a elles; porque velam por vossas almas, como aquelles que hão de dar conta d’ellas; para que o façam com alegria e não gemendo; porque isso não vos seria util.
texts.heb.13.18: Rogae por nós, porque confiamos que temos boa consciencia, como aquelles que em tudo querem portar-se honestamente.
texts.heb.13.19: E rogo-vos com instancia que assim o façaes, para que eu mais depressa vos seja restituido.
texts.heb.13.20: Ora o Deus de paz, que pelo sangue do concerto eterno tornou a trazer dos mortos a nosso Senhor Jesus Christo, grande pastor das ovelhas,
texts.heb.13.21: Vos aperfeiçoe em toda a boa obra, para fazerdes a sua vontade, obrando em vós o que perante elle é agradavel por Christo Jesus, ao qual seja gloria para todo o sempre. Amen.
texts.heb.13.22: Rogo-vos, porém, irmãos, que supporteis a palavra d’esta exhortação; porque abreviadamente vos escrevi.
texts.heb.13.23: Sabei que já está solto o irmão Timotheo, com o qual (se vier depressa) vos verei.
texts.heb.13.24: Saudae a todos os vossos chefes e a todos os sanctos. Os de Italia vos saudam.
texts.heb.13.25: A graça seja com todos vós. Amen.

texts.heb.1.1: God, who at sundry times and in divers manners spoke in time past to the fathers by the prophets,
texts.heb.1.2: Hath in these last days spoken to us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the worlds;
texts.heb.1.3: Who being the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person, and upholding all things by the word of his power, when he had by himself made purification of our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high;
texts.heb.1.4: Being made so much better than the angels, as he hath by inheritance obtained a more excellent name than they.
texts.heb.1.5: For to which of the angels said he at any time, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee? And again, I will be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Son?
texts.heb.1.6: And again, when he bringeth in the first-begotten into the world, he saith, And let all the angels of God worship him.
texts.heb.1.7: And of the angels he saith, Who maketh his angels spirits, and his ministers a flame of fire.
texts.heb.1.8: But to the Son, he saith, Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: a scepter of righteousness is the scepter of thy kingdom.
texts.heb.1.9: Thou hast loved righteousness, and hated iniquity; therefore God, even thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.
texts.heb.1.10: And, Thou, Lord, in the beginning hast laid the foundation of the earth: and the heavens are the works of thy hands.
texts.heb.1.11: They shall perish; but thou remainest: and they all shall become old as doth a garment;
texts.heb.1.12: And as a vesture wilt thou fold them up, and they shall be changed; but thou art the same, and thy years shall not fail.
texts.heb.1.13: But to which of the angels said he at any time, Sit on my right hand, until I make thy enemies thy footstool?
texts.heb.1.14: Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall inherit salvation?
texts.heb.2.1: Therefore we ought to give the more earnest heed to the things which we have heard, lest at any time we should let them slip.
texts.heb.2.2: For if the word spoken by angels was steadfast, and every transgression and disobedience received a just recompense of reward;
texts.heb.2.3: How shall we escape, if we neglect so great salvation; which at the first began to be spoken by the Lord, and was confirmed to us by them that heard him;
texts.heb.2.4: God also bearing them testimony, both with signs and wonders, and with divers miracles, and gifts of the Holy Spirit, according to his own will?
texts.heb.2.5: For to the angels he hath not put in subjection the world to come, concerning which we speak.
texts.heb.2.6: But one in a certain place testified, saying, What is man, that thou art mindful of him? or the son of man, that thou visitest him?
texts.heb.2.7: Thou madest him a little lower than the angels; thou crownedst him with glory and honor, and didst set him over the works of thy hands:
texts.heb.2.8: Thou hast put all things in subjection under his feet. For in that he put all in subjection under him, he left nothing that is not made subject to him. But now we see not yet all things subjected to him.
texts.heb.2.9: But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honor; that he by the grace of God should taste death for every man.
texts.heb.2.10: For it became him, for whom are all things, and by whom are all things, in bringing many sons to glory, to make the Captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings.
texts.heb.2.11: For both he that sanctifieth, and they who are sanctified, are all of one: for which cause he is not ashamed to call them brethren,
texts.heb.2.12: Saying, I will declare thy name to my brethren, in the midst of the church will I sing praise to thee.
texts.heb.2.13: And again, I will put my trust in him. And again, Behold, I, and the children which God hath given me.
texts.heb.2.14: Since then the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself likewise took part of the same; that through death he might destroy him that had the power of death, that is, the devil;
texts.heb.2.15: And deliver them, who, through fear of death, were all their life-time subject to bondage.
texts.heb.2.16: For verily he took not on him the nature of angels; but he took on him the seed of Abraham.
texts.heb.2.17: Wherefore in all things it behooved him to be made like his brethren; that he might be a merciful and faithful High Priest in things pertaining to God, to make reconciliation for the sins of the people.
texts.heb.2.18: For in that he himself hath suffered, being tempted, he is able to succor them that are tempted.
texts.heb.3.1: Wherefore, holy brethren, partakers of the heavenly calling, consider the Apostle and High Priest of our profession, Christ Jesus;
texts.heb.3.2: Who was faithful to him that appointed him, as also Moses was faithful in all his house.
texts.heb.3.3: For this man was counted worthy of more glory than Moses, inasmuch as he who hath built the house, hath more honor than the house.
texts.heb.3.4: For every house is built by some man; but he that built all things is God.
texts.heb.3.5: And Moses verily was faithful in all his house, as a servant, for a testimony of those things which were afterwards to be spoken.
texts.heb.3.6: But Christ as a son over his own house: whose house are we, if we hold fast the confidence, and the rejoicing of the hope firm to the end.
texts.heb.3.7: Wherefore (as the Holy Spirit saith, To-day if ye will hear his voice,
texts.heb.3.8: Harden not your hearts, as in the provocation, in the day of temptation in the wilderness:
texts.heb.3.9: When your fathers tempted me, proved me, and saw my works forty years.
texts.heb.3.10: Wherefore I was grieved with that generation, and said, They do always err in their heart; and they have not known my ways.
texts.heb.3.11: So I swore in my wrath, They shall not enter into my rest.)
texts.heb.3.12: Take heed, brethren, lest there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief, in departing from the living God.
texts.heb.3.13: But exhort one another daily, while it is called To-day; lest any of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin.
texts.heb.3.14: For we are made partakers of Christ, if we hold the beginning of our confidence steadfast to the end;
texts.heb.3.15: While it is said, To-day if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts, as in the provocation.
texts.heb.3.16: For some, when they had heard, did provoke: yet, not all that came out of Egypt by Moses.
texts.heb.3.17: But with whom was he grieved forty years? was it not with them that had sinned, whose carcasses fell in the wilderness?
texts.heb.3.18: And to whom did he swear that they should not enter into his rest, but to them that believed not?
texts.heb.3.19: So we see that they could not enter in because of unbelief.
texts.heb.4.1: Let us therefore fear, lest a promise being left us of entering into his rest, any of you should seem to come short of it.
texts.heb.4.2: For to us was the gospel preached, as well as to them: but the word which they heard did not profit them, not being mixed with faith in them that heard it.
texts.heb.4.3: For we who have believed do enter into rest, as he said, As I have sworn in my wrath, if they shall enter into my rest: although the works were finished from the foundation of the world.
texts.heb.4.4: For he spoke in a certain place of the seventh day on this wise, And God rested the seventh day from all his works.
texts.heb.4.5: And in this place again, If they shall enter into my rest.
texts.heb.4.6: Seeing therefore it remaineth that some must enter into it, and they to whom it was first preached entered not because of unbelief:
texts.heb.4.7: (Again, he limiteth a certain day, saying in David, To-day, after so long a time; as it is said, To-day, if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts.
texts.heb.4.8: For if Jesus had given them rest, then he would not afterward have spoken of another day.
texts.heb.4.9: There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God.
texts.heb.4.10: For he that hath entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his.)
texts.heb.4.11: Let us labor therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief.
texts.heb.4.12: For the word of God is living, and powerful, and sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.
texts.heb.4.13: Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened to the eyes of him with whom we have to do.
texts.heb.4.14: Seeing then that we have a great High Priest, that hath passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast our profession.
texts.heb.4.15: For we have not a high priest who cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but who was in all points tempted as we are, yet without sin.
texts.heb.4.16: Let us therefore come boldly to the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need.
texts.heb.5.1: For every high priest taken from among men, is ordained for men in things pertaining to God, that he may offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins:
texts.heb.5.2: Who can have compassion on the ignorant, and on them that are out of the way; for that he himself also is compassed with infirmity.
texts.heb.5.3: And by reason of this he ought, as for the people, so also for himself, to offer for sins.
texts.heb.5.4: And no man taketh this honor to himself, but he that is called by God, as was Aaron:
texts.heb.5.5: So also Christ glorified not himself to be made a high priest; but he that said to him, Thou art my Son, to-day have I begotten thee.
texts.heb.5.6: As he saith also in another place, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.
texts.heb.5.7: Who in the days of his flesh, when he had offered up prayers and supplications with strong crying and tears to him that was able to save him from death, and was heard, in that he feared;
texts.heb.5.8: Though he was a Son, yet he learned obedience by the things which he suffered;
texts.heb.5.9: And being made perfect, he became the author of eternal salvation to all them that obey him;
texts.heb.5.10: Called by God a high priest after the order of Melchisedec.
texts.heb.5.11: Of whom we have many things to say, and hard to be uttered, seeing ye are dull of hearing.
texts.heb.5.12: For when for the time ye ought to be teachers, ye have need of one to teach you again which are the first principles of the oracles of God; and are become such as have need of milk, and not of strong food.
texts.heb.5.13: For every one that useth milk, is unskillful in the word of righteousness: for he is a babe.
texts.heb.5.14: But strong food belongeth to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil.
texts.heb.6.1: Therefore leaving the principles of the doctrine of Christ, let us go on to perfection; not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works, and of faith towards God,
texts.heb.6.2: Of the doctrine of baptisms, and of laying on of hands, and of the resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment.
texts.heb.6.3: And this will we do, if God permit.
texts.heb.6.4: For it is impossible for those who have been once enlightened, and have tasted the heavenly gift, and have been made partakers of the Holy Spirit.
texts.heb.6.5: And have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come,
texts.heb.6.6: If they shall fall away, to renew them again to repentance; seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame.
texts.heb.6.7: For the earth which drinketh in the rain that cometh often upon it, and bringeth forth herbs fit for them by whom it is dressed, receiveth blessing from God:
texts.heb.6.8: But that which beareth thorns and briers is rejected, and is nigh to cursing; whose end is to be burned.
texts.heb.6.9: But, beloved, we are persuaded better things of you, and things that accompany salvation, though we thus speak.
texts.heb.6.10: For God is not unrighteous to forget your work and labor of love, which ye have shown towards his name, in that ye have ministered to the saints, and do minister.
texts.heb.6.11: And we desire every one of you to show the same diligence to the full assurance of hope to the end:
texts.heb.6.12: That ye be not slothful, but followers of them who through faith and patience inherit the promises.
texts.heb.6.13: For when God made promise to Abraham, because he could swear by no greater, he swore by himself,
texts.heb.6.14: Saying, Surely blessing I will bless thee, and multiplying I will multiply thee.
texts.heb.6.15: And so, after he had patiently endured, he obtained the promise.
texts.heb.6.16: For men verily swear by the greater: and an oath for confirmation is to them an end of all contradiction.
texts.heb.6.17: Wherein God, willing more abundantly to show to the heirs of promise the immutability of his counsel, confirmed it by an oath:
texts.heb.6.18: That by two immutable things, in which it was impossible for God to lie, we might have a strong consolation, who have fled for refuge to lay hold upon the hope set before us:
texts.heb.6.19: Which hope we have as an anchor of the soul, both sure and steadfast, and which entereth into that within the vail;
texts.heb.6.20: Whither the forerunner hath for us entered, even Jesus, made a high priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.
texts.heb.7.1: For this Melchisedec, king of Salem, priest of the most high God, who met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings, and blessed him;
texts.heb.7.2: To whom also Abraham gave a tenth part of all; first being by interpretation King of righteousness, and after that also King of Salem, which is, King of peace;
texts.heb.7.3: Without father, without mother, without descent, having neither beginning of days, nor end of life; but made like to the Son of God; abideth a priest continually.
texts.heb.7.4: Now consider how great this man was, to whom even the patriarch Abraham gave the tenth of the spoils.
texts.heb.7.5: And verily they that are of the sons of Levi, who receive the office of the priesthood, have a commandment to take tithes from the people according to the law, that is, from their brethren, though they come from the loins of Abraham:
texts.heb.7.6: But he whose descent is not counted from them received tithes from Abraham, and blessed him that had the promises.
texts.heb.7.7: And without all contradiction the less is blessed by the better.
texts.heb.7.8: And here men that die receive tithes; but there he receiveth them, of whom it is testified that he liveth.
texts.heb.7.9: And as I may say, Levi also, who receiveth tithes, payed tithes in Abraham.
texts.heb.7.10: For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him.
texts.heb.7.11: If therefore perfection were by the Levitical priesthood (for under it the people received the law) what further need was there that another priest should rise after the order of Melchisedec, and not be called after the order of Aaron?
texts.heb.7.12: For the priesthood being changed, there is made of necessity a change also of the law.
texts.heb.7.13: For he of whom these things are spoken pertaineth to another tribe, of which no man gave attendance at the altar.
texts.heb.7.14: For it is evident that our Lord sprang from Judah; of which tribe Moses spoke nothing concerning priesthood.
texts.heb.7.15: And it is yet far more evident: for that after the similitude of Melchisedec there ariseth another priest,
texts.heb.7.16: Who is made, not after the law of a carnal commandment, but after the power of an endless life.
texts.heb.7.17: For he testifieth, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.
texts.heb.7.18: For there is verily a disannulling of the preceding commandment on account of its weakness and unprofitableness.
texts.heb.7.19: For the law made nothing perfect, but the introduction of a better hope did; by which we draw nigh to God.
texts.heb.7.20: And inasmuch as not without an oath he was made priest:
texts.heb.7.21: (For those priests were made without an oath; but this with an oath, by him that said to him, The Lord swore, and will not repent, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec:)
texts.heb.7.22: By so much was Jesus made a surety of a better testament.
texts.heb.7.23: And they truly were many priests, because they were not suffered to continue by reason of death:
texts.heb.7.24: But this man, because he continueth ever, hath an unchangeable priesthood.
texts.heb.7.25: Wherefore he is able also to save them to the uttermost that come to God by him, seeing he ever liveth to make intercession for them.
texts.heb.7.26: For such a high priest became us, who is holy, harmless, undefiled, separate from sinners, and made higher than the heavens;
texts.heb.7.27: Who needeth not daily, as those high priests, to offer up sacrifice, first for his own sins, and then for the people's: for this he did once, when he offered up himself.
texts.heb.7.28: For the law maketh men high priests who have infirmity; but the word of the oath, which was after the law, maketh the Son, who is consecrated for evermore.
texts.heb.8.1: Now of the things which we have spoken this is the sum: We have such a high priest, who is set on the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens;
texts.heb.8.2: A minister of the sanctuary, and of the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, and not man.
texts.heb.8.3: For every high priest is ordained to offer gifts and sacrifices: wherefore it is of necessity that this man should have somewhat also to offer.
texts.heb.8.4: For if he were on earth, he would not be a priest, seeing there are priests that offer gifts according to the law:
texts.heb.8.5: Who serve to the example and shadow of heavenly things, as Moses was admonished by God when he was about to make the tabernacle: for, See (saith he) that thou make all things according to the pattern shown to thee in the mount.
texts.heb.8.6: But now hath he obtained a more excellent ministry, by how much also he is the mediator of a better covenant, which was established upon better promises.
texts.heb.8.7: For if that first covenant had been faultless, then would no place have been sought for the second.
texts.heb.8.8: For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah:
texts.heb.8.9: Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers, in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord.
texts.heb.8.10: For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord; I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people:
texts.heb.8.11: And they shall not teach every man his neighbor, and every man his brother, saying, Know the Lord: for all shall know me, from the least to the greatest.
texts.heb.8.12: For I will be merciful to their unrighteousness, and their sins and their iniquities will I remember no more.
texts.heb.8.13: In that he saith, A new covenant, he hath made the first old. Now that which decayeth and groweth old is ready to vanish away.
texts.heb.9.1: Then verily the first covenant had also ordinances of divine service, and a worldly sanctuary.
texts.heb.9.2: For there was a tabernacle made; the first, in which was the candlestick, and the table, and the show-bread; which is called the sanctuary.
texts.heb.9.3: And after the second vail, the tabernacle which is called the Holiest of all;
texts.heb.9.4: Which had the golden censer, and the ark of the covenant overlaid around with gold, in which was the golden pot that had manna, and Aaron's rod that budded, and the tables of the covenant;
texts.heb.9.5: And over it the cherubim of glory shadowing the mercy-seat; of which we cannot now speak particularly.
texts.heb.9.6: Now when these things were thus ordained, the priests went always into the first tabernacle, accomplishing the service of God:
texts.heb.9.7: But into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood, which he offered for himself, and for the errors of the people:
texts.heb.9.8: The Holy Spirit this signifying, that the way into the holiest of all was not yet made manifest, while the first tabernacle was yet standing:
texts.heb.9.9: Which was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience;
texts.heb.9.10: Which stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation.
texts.heb.9.11: But Christ being come a high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building;
texts.heb.9.12: Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood; he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us.
texts.heb.9.13: For if the blood of bulls and of goats, and the ashes of a heifer sprinkling the unclean, sanctify to the purifying of the flesh:
texts.heb.9.14: How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, cleanse your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?
texts.heb.9.15: And for this cause he is the mediator of the new testament, that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament, they who are called may receive the promise of eternal inheritance.
texts.heb.9.16: For where a testament is, there must also of necessity be the death of the testator.
texts.heb.9.17: For a testament is of force after men are dead: otherwise it is of no strength at all while the testator liveth.
texts.heb.9.18: Hence even the first testament was not dedicated without blood.
texts.heb.9.19: For when Moses had spoken every precept to all the people according to the law, he took the blood of calves and of goats, with water, and scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book and all the people,
texts.heb.9.20: Saying, This is the blood of the testament which God hath enjoined to you.
texts.heb.9.21: Moreover, he sprinkled likewise with blood both the tabernacle, and all the vessels of the ministry.
texts.heb.9.22: And almost all things are by the law cleansed with blood; and without shedding of blood is no remission.
texts.heb.9.23: It was therefore necessary that the patterns of things in the heavens should be purified with these; but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.
texts.heb.9.24: For Christ hath not entered into the holy places made with hands, which are the figures of the true; but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us:
texts.heb.9.25: Nor yet that he should offer himself often, as the high priest entereth into the holy place every year with blood of others;
texts.heb.9.26: For then must he often have suffered since the foundation of the world: but now once in the end of the world hath he appeared to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself.
texts.heb.9.27: And as it is appointed to men once to die, but after this the judgment:
texts.heb.9.28: So Christ was once offered to bear the sins of many; and to them that look for him he will appear the second time without sin to salvation.
texts.heb.10.1: For the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers to them perfect.
texts.heb.10.2: For then would they not have ceased to be offered? because that the worshipers once cleansed, would have had no more conscience of sins.
texts.heb.10.3: But in those sacrifices there is a remembrance again made of sins every year.
texts.heb.10.4: For it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins.
texts.heb.10.5: Wherefore, when he cometh into the world, he saith, Sacrifice and offering thou wouldst not, but a body hast thou prepared me:
texts.heb.10.6: In burnt-offerings and sacrifices for sin thou hast had no pleasure.
texts.heb.10.7: Then said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written concerning me,) to do thy will, O God.
texts.heb.10.8: Above, when he said, Sacrifice and offering and burnt-offerings and offering for sin thou wouldst not, neither hadst pleasure in them; which are offered by the law;
texts.heb.10.9: Then said he, Lo, I come to do thy will, O God. He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second.
texts.heb.10.10: By which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
texts.heb.10.11: And every priest standeth daily ministering and offering often the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins:
texts.heb.10.12: But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins, for ever sat down on the right hand of God;
texts.heb.10.13: From henceforth waiting till his enemies are made his footstool.
texts.heb.10.14: For by one offering he hath perfected for ever them that are sanctified.
texts.heb.10.15: Of this the Holy Spirit also is a witness to us: for after that he had said before,
texts.heb.10.16: This is the covenant that I will make with them after those days, saith the Lord, I will put my laws into their hearts, and in their minds will I write them;
texts.heb.10.17: And their sins and iniquities will I remember no more.
texts.heb.10.18: Now where remission of these is, there is no more offering for sin.
texts.heb.10.19: Having therefore, brethren, boldness to enter into the holiest by the blood of Jesus,
texts.heb.10.20: By a new and living way, which he hath consecrated for us, through the vail, that is to say, his flesh;
texts.heb.10.21: And having a high priest over the house of God;
texts.heb.10.22: Let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, and our bodies washed with pure water.
texts.heb.10.23: Let us hold fast the profession of our faith without wavering; for he is faithful that promised:
texts.heb.10.24: And let us consider one another to excite to love and to good works:
texts.heb.10.25: Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching.
texts.heb.10.26: For if we sin willfully after we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins,
texts.heb.10.27: But a certain fearful apprehension of judgment and fiery indignation, which shall devour the adversaries.
texts.heb.10.28: He that despised Moses' law, died without mercy under two or three witnesses:
texts.heb.10.29: Of how much more severe punishment, suppose ye, shall he be thought worthy, who hath trodden under foot the Son of God, and hath counted the blood of the covenant, by which he was sanctified, an unholy thing, and hath done despite to the Spirit of grace?
texts.heb.10.30: For we know him that hath said, Vengeance belongeth to me, I will recompense, saith the Lord. And again, The Lord will judge his people.
texts.heb.10.31: It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
texts.heb.10.32: But call to remembrance the former days, in which, after ye were illuminated, ye endured a great fight of afflictions;
texts.heb.10.33: Partly, while ye were made a gazing-stock both by reproaches and afflictions; and partly, while ye became companions of them that were so used.
texts.heb.10.34: For ye had compassion of me in my bonds, and took joyfully the seizing of your goods, knowing in yourselves that ye have in heaven a better and an enduring substance.
texts.heb.10.35: Cast not away therefore your confidence, which hath great recompense of reward.
texts.heb.10.36: For ye have need of patience, that, after ye have done the will of God, ye may receive the promise.
texts.heb.10.37: For yet a little while, and he that is coming will come, and will not tarry.
texts.heb.10.38: Now the just shall live by faith: but if any man shall draw back, my soul shall have no pleasure in him.
texts.heb.10.39: But we are not of them who draw back to perdition; but of them that believe to the saving of the soul.
texts.heb.11.1: Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.
texts.heb.11.2: For by it the elders obtained a good report.
texts.heb.11.3: Through faith we understand that the worlds were framed by the word of God, so that things which are seen were not made of things which appeared.
texts.heb.11.4: By faith Abel offered to God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained testimony that he was righteous, God testifying of his gifts: and by it he being dead yet speaketh.
texts.heb.11.5: By faith Enoch was translated, that he should not see death; and was not found, because God had translated him: for before his translation he had this testimony, that he pleased God.
texts.heb.11.6: But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.
texts.heb.11.7: By faith Noah, being warned by God of things not seen as yet, moved with fear, prepared an ark to the saving of his house; by which he condemned the world, and became heir of the righteousness which is by faith.
texts.heb.11.8: By faith Abraham, when he was called to remove into a place which he should afterwards receive for an inheritance, obeyed; and he went out not knowing whither he was going.
texts.heb.11.9: By faith he sojourned in the land of promise, as in a foreign country, dwelling in tabernacles with Isaac and Jacob, the heirs with him of the same promise:
texts.heb.11.10: For he looked for a city which hath foundations, whose builder and maker is God.
texts.heb.11.11: Through faith also Sarah herself received strength to conceive seed, and was delivered of a child when she was past age, because she judged him faithful who had promised.
texts.heb.11.12: Therefore there sprang even from one, and him as good as dead, so many as the stars of the sky in multitude, and as the sand which is by the sea-shore innumerable.
texts.heb.11.13: These all died in faith, not having received the promises, but having seen them afar off, and were persuaded of them, and embraced them, and confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth.
texts.heb.11.14: For they that say such things declare plainly that they seek a country.
texts.heb.11.15: And truly, if they had been mindful of that country from whence they came, they might have had opportunity to return.
texts.heb.11.16: But now they desire a better country, that is, a heavenly: wherefore God is not ashamed to be called their God; for he hath prepared for them a city.
texts.heb.11.17: By faith Abraham, when he was tried, offered up Isaac: and he that had received the promises offered up his only-begotten son,
texts.heb.11.18: Of whom it was said, That in Isaac shall thy seed be called:
texts.heb.11.19: Accounting that God was able to raise him even from the dead; from whence also he received him in a figure.
texts.heb.11.20: By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau concerning things to come.
texts.heb.11.21: By faith Jacob, when he was dying, blessed both the sons of Joseph; and worshiped, leaning upon the top of his staff.
texts.heb.11.22: By faith Joseph, when he died, made mention of the departing of the children of Israel; and gave commandment concerning his bones.
texts.heb.11.23: By faith Moses when he was born, was hid three months by his parents, because they saw he was a proper child; and they were not afraid of the king's commandment.
texts.heb.11.24: By faith Moses, when he had come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter;
texts.heb.11.25: Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season;
texts.heb.11.26: Esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures of Egypt: for he had respect to the recompense of the reward.
texts.heb.11.27: By faith he forsook Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king: for he endured, as seeing him who is invisible.
texts.heb.11.28: Through faith he kept the passover, and the sprinkling of blood, lest he that destroyed the first-born should touch them.
texts.heb.11.29: By faith they passed through the Red sea as by dry land: which the Egyptians essaying to do were drowned.
texts.heb.11.30: By faith the walls of Jericho fell down after they had been encompassed seven days.
texts.heb.11.31: By faith the harlot Rahab perished not with them that believed not, as she had received the spies with peace.
texts.heb.11.32: And what shall I say more? for the time would fail me to tell of Gideon, and of Barak, and of Samson, and of Jephthah, of David also, and Samuel, and of the prophets:
texts.heb.11.33: Who through faith subdued kingdoms, wrought righteousness, obtained promises, stopped the mouths of lions,
texts.heb.11.34: Quenched the violence of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, out of weakness were made strong, became valiant in fight, turned to flight the armies of the aliens.
texts.heb.11.35: Women received their dead raised to life again: and others were tortured, not accepting deliverance; that they might obtain a better resurrection:
texts.heb.11.36: And others had trial of cruel mockings and scourgings, and, moreover of bonds and imprisonment:
texts.heb.11.37: They were stoned, they were sawn asunder, were tempted, were slain with the sword: they wandered about in sheep-skins, and goat-skins; being destitute, afflicted, tormented;
texts.heb.11.38: (Of whom the world was not worthy:) they wandered in deserts, and in mountains, and in dens and caves of the earth.
texts.heb.11.39: And these all, having obtained a good report through faith, received not the promise:
texts.heb.11.40: God having provided some better thing for us, that they without us should not be made perfect.
texts.heb.12.1: Wherefore, seeing we also are encompassed with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us,
texts.heb.12.2: Looking to Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God.
texts.heb.12.3: For consider him that endured such contradiction of sinners against himself, lest ye be wearied and faint in your minds.
texts.heb.12.4: Ye have not yet resisted to blood, striving against sin.
texts.heb.12.5: And ye have forgotten the exhortation which speaketh to you as to children, My son, despise not thou the chastening of the Lord, nor faint when thou art rebuked by him:
texts.heb.12.6: For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth.
texts.heb.12.7: If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons: for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not?
texts.heb.12.8: But if ye are without chastisement, of which all are partakers, then are ye bastards and not sons.
texts.heb.12.9: Furthermore, we have had fathers of our flesh who corrected us, and we gave them reverence: shall we not much rather be in subjection to the Father of spirits, and live?
texts.heb.12.10: For they verily for a few days chastened us after their own pleasure; but he for our profit, that we might be partakers of his holiness.
texts.heb.12.11: Now no chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous, but grievous: nevertheless, afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness to them who are exercised by it.
texts.heb.12.12: Wherefore lift up the hands which hang down, and the feeble knees;
texts.heb.12.13: And make straight paths for your feet, lest that which is lame be turned out of the way; but let it rather be healed.
texts.heb.12.14: Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord:
texts.heb.12.15: Looking diligently, lest any man fail of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up, trouble you, and by it many be defiled;
texts.heb.12.16: Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of food sold his birth-right.
texts.heb.12.17: For ye know that afterward, when he would have inherited the blessing, he was rejected: for he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears.
texts.heb.12.18: For ye are not come to the mount that might be touched, and that burned with fire, nor to blackness, and to darkness, and tempest,
texts.heb.12.19: And the sound of a trumpet, and the voice of words; which voice they that heard, entreated that the word should not be spoken to them any more:
texts.heb.12.20: (For they could not endure that which was commanded, And if so much as a beast touch the mountain, it shall be stoned, or thrust through with a dart:
texts.heb.12.21: And so terrible was the sight, that Moses said, I exceedingly fear and tremble:)
texts.heb.12.22: But ye are come to mount Sion, and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to an innumerable company of angels,
texts.heb.12.23: To the general assembly and church of the first-born, who are written in heaven, and to God the Judge of all, and to the spirits of just men made perfect,
texts.heb.12.24: And to Jesus the mediator of the new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling, that speaketh better things than that of Abel.
texts.heb.12.25: See that ye refuse not him that speaketh. For if they escaped not who refused him that spoke on earth, much more shall not we escape, if we turn away from him that speaketh from heaven:
texts.heb.12.26: Whose voice then shook the earth: but now he hath promised, saying, Yet once more I shake not the earth only, but also heaven.
texts.heb.12.27: And this word, Yet once more, signifieth the removing of those things that are shaken, as of things that are made, that those things which cannot be shaken may remain.
texts.heb.12.28: Wherefore we receiving a kingdom which cannot be moved, let us have grace, by which we may serve God acceptably, with reverence and godly fear.
texts.heb.12.29: For our God is a consuming fire.
texts.heb.13.2: Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for by this some have entertained angels unawares.
texts.heb.13.3: Remember them that are in bonds, as bound with them; and them who suffer adversity, as being yourselves also in the body.
texts.heb.13.4: Marriage is honorable in all, and the bed undefiled: but lewd persons and adulterers God will judge.
texts.heb.13.5: Let your manner of life be without covetousness; and be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.
texts.heb.13.6: So that we may boldly say, The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear what man shall do to me.
texts.heb.13.7: Remember them who have the rule over you, who have spoken to you the word of God: whose faith follow, considering the end of their manner of life.
texts.heb.13.8: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to-day, and for ever.
texts.heb.13.9: Be not carried about with divers and strange doctrines: for it is a good thing that the heart be established with grace; not with meats, which have not profited them that have been occupied in them.
texts.heb.13.10: We have an altar, of which they have no right to eat who serve the tabernacle.
texts.heb.13.11: For the bodies of those beasts, whose blood is brought into the sanctuary by the high priest for sin, are burned without the camp.
texts.heb.13.12: Wherefore Jesus also, that he might sanctify the people with his own blood, suffered without the gate.
texts.heb.13.13: Let us go forth therefore to him without the camp, bearing his reproach.
texts.heb.13.14: For here we have no continuing city, but we seek one to come.
texts.heb.13.15: By him therefore let us offer the sacrifice of praise to God continually, that is, the fruit of our lips, giving thanks to his name.
texts.heb.13.16: But to do good, and to communicate, forget not: for with such sacrifices God is well pleased.
texts.heb.13.17: Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls, as they that must give account, that they may do it with joy, and not with grief: for that is unprofitable for you.
texts.heb.13.18: Pray for us: for we trust we have a good conscience, in all things willing to live honestly.
texts.heb.13.19: But I beseech you the rather to do this, that I may be restored to you the sooner.
texts.heb.13.20: Now the God of peace, that brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great Shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the everlasting covenant,
texts.heb.13.21: Make you perfect in every good work to do his will, working in you that which is well-pleasing in his sight, through Jesus Christ; to whom be glory for ever and ever. Amen.
texts.heb.13.22: And I beseech you, brethren, suffer the word of exhortation: for I have written a letter to you in few words.
texts.heb.13.23: Know ye, that our brother Timothy is set at liberty; with whom, if he come shortly, I will see you.
texts.heb.13.24: Salute all them that have the rule over you, and all the saints. They of Italy salute you.
texts.heb.13.25: Grace be with you all. Amen.

texts.heb.1.1: God having spoken in many parts and in many ways formerly to the fathers in the prophets,
texts.heb.1.2: at the end of these days has spoken to us in [the person of the] Son, whom he has established heir of all things, by whom also he made the worlds;
texts.heb.1.3: who being [the] effulgence of his glory and [the] expression of his substance, and upholding all things by the word of his power, having made [by himself] the purification of sins, set himself down on the right hand of the greatness on high,
texts.heb.1.4: taking a place by so much better than the angels, as he inherits a name more excellent than they.
texts.heb.1.5: For to which of the angels said he ever, *Thou* art my Son: this day have *I* begotten thee? and again, *I* will be to him for father, and *he* shall be to me for son?
texts.heb.1.6: and again, when he brings in the firstborn into the habitable world, he says, And let all God's angels worship him.
texts.heb.1.7: And as to the angels he says, Who makes his angels spirits and his ministers a flame of fire;
texts.heb.1.8: but as to the Son, Thy throne, O God, [is] to the age of the age, and a sceptre of uprightness [is] the sceptre of thy kingdom.
texts.heb.1.9: Thou hast loved righteousness and hast hated lawlessness; therefore God, thy God, has anointed thee with oil of gladness above thy companions.
texts.heb.1.10: And, *Thou* in the beginning, Lord, hast founded the earth, and works of thy hands are the heavens.
texts.heb.1.11: They shall perish, but *thou* continuest still; and they all shall grow old as a garment,
texts.heb.1.12: and as a covering shalt thou roll them up, and they shall be changed; but *thou* art the Same, and thy years shall not fail.
texts.heb.1.13: But as to which of the angels said he ever, Sit at my right hand until I put thine enemies [as] footstool of thy feet?
texts.heb.1.14: Are they not all ministering spirits, sent out for service on account of those who shall inherit salvation?
texts.heb.2.1: For this reason we should give heed more abundantly to the things [we have] heard, lest in any way we should slip away.
texts.heb.2.2: For if the word which was spoken by angels was firm, and every transgression and disobedience received just retribution,
texts.heb.2.3: how shall *we* escape if we have been negligent of so great salvation, which, having had its commencement in being spoken [of] by the Lord, has been confirmed to us by those who have heard;
texts.heb.2.4: God bearing, besides, witness with [them] to [it], both by signs and wonders, and various acts of power, and distributions of [the] Holy Spirit, according to his will?
texts.heb.2.5: For he has not subjected to angels the habitable world which is to come, of which we speak;
texts.heb.2.6: but one has testified somewhere, saying, What is man, that thou rememberest him, or son of man that thou visitest him?
texts.heb.2.7: Thou hast made him some little inferior to the angels; thou hast crowned him with glory and honour, [and hast set him over the works of thy hands;]
texts.heb.2.8: thou hast subjected all things under his feet. For in subjecting all things to him, he has left nothing unsubject to him. But now we see not yet all things subjected to *him*,
texts.heb.2.9: but we see Jesus, who [was] made some little inferior to angels on account of the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour; so that by the grace of God he should taste death for every thing.
texts.heb.2.10: For it became him, for whom [are] all things, and by whom [are] all things, in bringing many sons to glory, to make perfect the leader of their salvation through sufferings.
texts.heb.2.11: For both he that sanctifies and those sanctified [are] all of one; for which cause he is not ashamed to call them brethren,
texts.heb.2.12: saying, I will declare thy name to my brethren; in [the] midst of [the] assembly will I sing thy praises.
texts.heb.2.13: And again, I will trust in him. And again, Behold, I and the children which God has given me.
texts.heb.2.14: Since therefore the children partake of blood and flesh, he also, in like manner, took part in the same, that through death he might annul him who has the might of death, that is, the devil;
texts.heb.2.15: and might set free all those who through fear of death through the whole of their life were subject to bondage.
texts.heb.2.16: For he does not indeed take hold of angels [by the hand], but he takes hold of the seed of Abraham.
texts.heb.2.17: Wherefore it behoved him in all things to be made like to [his] brethren, that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest in things relating to God, to make propitiation for the sins of the people;
texts.heb.2.18: for, in that himself has suffered, being tempted, he is able to help those that are being tempted.
texts.heb.3.1: Wherefore, holy brethren, partakers of [the] heavenly calling, consider the Apostle and High Priest of our confession, Jesus,
texts.heb.3.2: who is faithful to him that has constituted him, as Moses also in all his house.
texts.heb.3.3: For *he* has been counted worthy of greater glory than Moses, by how much he that has built it has more honour than the house.
texts.heb.3.4: For every house is built by some one; but he who has built all things [is] God.
texts.heb.3.5: And Moses indeed [was] faithful in all his house, as a ministering servant, for a testimony of the things to be spoken after;
texts.heb.3.6: but Christ, as Son over his house, whose house are *we*, if indeed we hold fast the boldness and the boast of hope firm to the end.
texts.heb.3.7: Wherefore, even as says the Holy Spirit, To-day if ye will hear his voice,
texts.heb.3.8: harden not your hearts, as in the provocation, in the day of temptation in the wilderness;
texts.heb.3.9: where your fathers tempted [me], by proving [me], and saw my works forty years.
texts.heb.3.10: Wherefore I was wroth with this generation, and said, They always err in heart; and *they* have not known my ways;
texts.heb.3.11: so I swore in my wrath, If they shall enter into my rest.
texts.heb.3.12: See, brethren, lest there be in any one of you a wicked heart of unbelief, in turning away from [the] living God.
texts.heb.3.13: But encourage yourselves each day, as long as it is called To-day, that none of you be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin.
texts.heb.3.14: For we are become companions of the Christ if indeed we hold the beginning of the assurance firm to the end;
texts.heb.3.15: in that it is said, To-day if ye will hear his voice, do not harden your hearts, as in the provocation;
texts.heb.3.16: (for who was it, who, having heard, provoked? but [was it] not all who came out of Egypt by Moses?
texts.heb.3.17: And with whom was he wroth forty years? [Was it] not with those who had sinned, whose carcases fell in the wilderness?
texts.heb.3.18: And to whom sware he that they should not enter into his rest, but to those who had not hearkened to the word?
texts.heb.3.19: And we see that they could not enter in on account of unbelief;)
texts.heb.4.1: Let us therefore fear, lest, a promise being left of entering into his rest, any one of you might seem to have failed [of it].
texts.heb.4.2: For indeed we have had glad tidings presented to us, even as they also; but the word of the report did not profit *them*, not being mixed with faith in those who heard.
texts.heb.4.3: For we enter into the rest who have believed; as he said, As I have sworn in my wrath, If they shall enter into my rest; although the works had been completed from [the] foundation of [the] world.
texts.heb.4.4: For he has said somewhere of the seventh [day] thus, And God rested on the seventh day from all his works:
texts.heb.4.5: and in this again, If they shall enter into my rest.
texts.heb.4.6: Seeing therefore it remains that some enter into it, and those who first received the glad tidings did not enter in on account of not hearkening to the word,
texts.heb.4.7: again he determines a certain day, saying, in David, 'To-day,' after so long a time; (according as it has been said before), To-day, if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts.
texts.heb.4.8: For if Jesus had brought them into rest, he would not have spoken afterwards about another day.
texts.heb.4.9: There remains then a sabbatism to the people of God.
texts.heb.4.10: For he that has entered into his rest, he also has rested from his works, as God did from his own.
texts.heb.4.11: Let us therefore use diligence to enter into that rest, that no one may fall after the same example of not hearkening to the word.
texts.heb.4.12: For the word of God [is] living and operative, and sharper than any two-edged sword, and penetrating to [the] division of soul and spirit, both of joints and marrow, and a discerner of the thoughts and intents of [the] heart.
texts.heb.4.13: And there is not a creature unapparent before him; but all things [are] naked and laid bare to his eyes, with whom we have to do.
texts.heb.4.14: Having therefore a great high priest who has passed through the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast the confession.
texts.heb.4.15: For we have not a high priest not able to sympathise with our infirmities, but tempted in all things in like manner, sin apart.
texts.heb.4.16: Let us approach therefore with boldness to the throne of grace, that we may receive mercy, and find grace for seasonable help.
texts.heb.5.1: For every high priest taken from amongst men is established for men in things relating to God, that he may offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins;
texts.heb.5.2: being able to exercise forbearance towards the ignorant and erring, since he himself also is clothed with infirmity;
texts.heb.5.3: and, on account of this [infirmity], he ought, even as for the people, so also for himself, to offer for sins.
texts.heb.5.4: And no one takes the honour to himself but [as] called by God, even as Aaron also.
texts.heb.5.5: Thus the Christ also has not glorified himself to be made a high priest; but he who had said to him, *Thou* art my Son, *I* have to-day begotten thee.
texts.heb.5.6: Even as also in another [place] he says, *Thou* [art] a priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedec.
texts.heb.5.7: Who in the days of his flesh, having offered up both supplications and entreaties to him who was able to save him out of death, with strong crying and tears; (and having been heard because of his piety;)
texts.heb.5.8: though he were Son, he learned obedience from the things which he suffered;
texts.heb.5.9: and having been perfected, became to all them that obey him, author of eternal salvation;
texts.heb.5.10: addressed by God [as] high priest according to the order of Melchisedec.
texts.heb.5.11: Concerning whom we have much to say, and hard to be interpreted in speaking [of it], since ye are become dull in hearing.
texts.heb.5.12: For when for the time ye ought to be teachers, ye have again need that [one] should teach you what [are] the elements of the beginning of the oracles of God, and are become such as have need of milk, [and] not of solid food.
texts.heb.5.13: For every one that partakes of milk [is] unskilled in the word of righteousness, for he is a babe;
texts.heb.5.14: but solid food belongs to full-grown men, who, on account of habit, have their senses exercised for distinguishing both good and evil.
texts.heb.6.1: Wherefore, leaving the word of the beginning of the Christ, let us go on [to what belongs] to full growth, not laying again a foundation of repentance from dead works and faith in God,
texts.heb.6.2: of [the] doctrine of washings, and of imposition of hands, and of resurrection of [the] dead, and of eternal judgment;
texts.heb.6.3: and this will we do if God permit.
texts.heb.6.4: For it is impossible to renew again to repentance those once enlightened, and who have tasted of the heavenly gift, and have been made partakers of [the] Holy Spirit,
texts.heb.6.5: and have tasted the good word of God, and [the] works of power of [the] age to come,
texts.heb.6.6: and have fallen away, crucifying for themselves [as they do] the Son of God, and making a show of [him].
texts.heb.6.7: For ground which drinks the rain which comes often upon it, and produces useful herbs for those for whose sakes also it is tilled, partakes of blessing from God;
texts.heb.6.8: but bringing forth thorns and briars, it is found worthless and nigh to a curse, whose end [is] to be burned.
texts.heb.6.9: But we are persuaded concerning you, beloved, better things, and connected with salvation, even if we speak thus.
texts.heb.6.10: For God [is] not unrighteous to forget your work, and the love which ye have shewn to his name, having ministered to the saints, and [still] ministering.
texts.heb.6.11: But we desire earnestly that each one of you shew the same diligence to the full assurance of hope unto the end;
texts.heb.6.12: that ye be not sluggish, but imitators of those who through faith and patience have been inheritors of the promises.
texts.heb.6.13: For God, having promised to Abraham, since he had no greater to swear by, swore by himself,
texts.heb.6.14: saying, Surely blessing I will bless thee, and multiplying I will multiply thee;
texts.heb.6.15: and thus, having had long patience, he got the promise.
texts.heb.6.16: For men indeed swear by a greater, and with them the oath is a term to all dispute, as making matters sure.
texts.heb.6.17: Wherein God, willing to shew more abundantly to the heirs of the promise the unchangeableness of his purpose, intervened by an oath,
texts.heb.6.18: that by two unchangeable things, in which [it was] impossible that God should lie, we might have a strong encouragement, who have fled for refuge to lay hold on the hope set before us,
texts.heb.6.19: which we have as anchor of the soul, both secure and firm, and entering into that within the veil,
texts.heb.6.20: where Jesus is entered as forerunner for us, become for ever a high priest according to the order of Melchisedec.
texts.heb.7.1: For this Melchisedec, King of Salem, priest of the most high God, who met Abraham returning from smiting the kings, and blessed him;
texts.heb.7.2: to whom Abraham gave also the tenth portion of all; first being interpreted King of righteousness, and then also King of Salem, which is King of peace;
texts.heb.7.3: without father, without mother, without genealogy; having neither beginning of days nor end of life, but assimilated to the Son of God, abides a priest continually.
texts.heb.7.4: Now consider how great this [personage] was, to whom [even] the patriarch Abraham gave a tenth out of the spoils.
texts.heb.7.5: And they indeed from among the sons of Levi, who receive the priesthood, have commandment to take tithes from the people according to the law, that is from their brethren, though these are come out of the loins of Abraham:
texts.heb.7.6: but he who has no genealogy from them has tithed Abraham, and blessed him who had the promises.
texts.heb.7.7: But beyond all gainsaying, the inferior is blessed by the better.
texts.heb.7.8: And here dying men receive tithes; but there [one] of whom the witness is that he lives;
texts.heb.7.9: and, so to speak, through Abraham, Levi also, who received tithes, has been made to pay tithes.
texts.heb.7.10: For he was yet in the loins of his father when Melchisedec met him.
texts.heb.7.11: If indeed then perfection were by the Levitical priesthood, for the people had their law given to them in connexion with *it*, what need [was there] still that a different priest should arise according to the order of Melchisedec, and not be named after the order of Aaron?
texts.heb.7.12: For, the priesthood being changed, there takes place of necessity a change of law also.
texts.heb.7.13: For he, of whom these things are said, belongs to a different tribe, of which no one has [ever] been attached to the service of the altar.
texts.heb.7.14: For it is clear that our Lord has sprung out of Juda, as to which tribe Moses spake nothing as to priests.
texts.heb.7.15: And it is yet more abundantly evident, since a different priest arises according to the similitude of Melchisedec,
texts.heb.7.16: who has been constituted not according to law of fleshly commandment, but according to power of indissoluble life.
texts.heb.7.17: For it is borne witness, *Thou* art a priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedec.
texts.heb.7.18: For there is a setting aside of the commandment going before for its weakness and unprofitableness,
texts.heb.7.19: (for the law perfected nothing,) and the introduction of a better hope by which we draw nigh to God.
texts.heb.7.20: And by how much [it was] not without the swearing of an oath;
texts.heb.7.21: (for they are become priests without the swearing of an oath, but he with the swearing of an oath, by him who said, as to him, The Lord has sworn, and will not repent [of it], *Thou* [art] priest for ever [according to the order of Melchisedec];)
texts.heb.7.22: by so much Jesus became surety of a better covenant.
texts.heb.7.23: And they have been many priests, on account of being hindered from continuing by death;
texts.heb.7.24: but he, because of his continuing for ever, has the priesthood unchangeable.
texts.heb.7.25: Whence also he is able to save completely those who approach by him to God, always living to intercede for them.
texts.heb.7.26: For such a high priest became us, holy, harmless, undefiled, separated from sinners, and become higher than the heavens:
texts.heb.7.27: who has not day by day need, as the high priests, first to offer up sacrifices for his own sins, then [for] those of the people; for this he did once for all [in] having offered up himself.
texts.heb.7.28: For the law constitutes men high priests, having infirmity; but the word of the swearing of the oath which [is] after the law, a Son perfected for ever.
texts.heb.8.1: Now a summary of the things of which we are speaking [is], We have such a one high priest who has sat down on [the] right hand of the throne of the greatness in the heavens;
texts.heb.8.2: minister of the holy places and of the true tabernacle, which the Lord has pitched, [and] not man.
texts.heb.8.3: For every high priest is constituted for the offering both of gifts and sacrifices; whence it is needful that this one also should have something which he may offer.
texts.heb.8.4: If then indeed he were upon earth, he would not even be a priest, there being those who offer the gifts according to the law,
texts.heb.8.5: (who serve the representation and shadow of heavenly things, according as Moses was oracularly told [when] about to make the tabernacle; for See, saith He, that thou make all things according to the pattern which has been shewn to thee in the mountain.)
texts.heb.8.6: But now he has got a more excellent ministry, by so much as he is mediator of a better covenant, which is established on the footing of better promises.
texts.heb.8.7: For if that first was faultless, place had not been sought for a second.
texts.heb.8.8: For finding fault, he says to them, Behold, days come, saith the Lord, and I will consummate a new covenant as regards the house of Israel, and as regards the house of Juda;
texts.heb.8.9: not according to the covenant which I made to their fathers in [the] day of my taking their hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because *they* did not continue in my covenant, and *I* did not regard them, saith [the] Lord.
texts.heb.8.10: Because this [is] the covenant that I will covenant to the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord: Giving my laws into their mind, I will write them also upon their hearts; and I will be to them for God, and *they* shall be to me for people.
texts.heb.8.11: And they shall not teach each his fellow-citizen, and each his brother, saying, Know the Lord; because all shall know me in themselves, from [the] little one [among them] unto [the] great among them.
texts.heb.8.12: Because I will be merciful to their unrighteousnesses, and their sins and their lawlessnesses I will never remember any more.
texts.heb.8.13: In that he says New, he has made the first old; but that which grows old and aged [is] near disappearing.
texts.heb.9.1: The first therefore also indeed had ordinances of service, and the sanctuary, a worldly one.
texts.heb.9.2: For a tabernacle was set up; the first, in which [were] both the candlestick and the table and the exposition of the loaves, which is called Holy;
texts.heb.9.3: but after the second veil a tabernacle which is called Holy of holies,
texts.heb.9.4: having a golden censer, and the ark of the covenant, covered round in every part with gold, in which [were] the golden pot that had the manna, and the rod of Aaron that had sprouted, and the tables of the covenant;
texts.heb.9.5: and above over it the cherubim of glory shadowing the mercy-seat; concerning which it is not now [the time] to speak in detail.
texts.heb.9.6: Now these things being thus ordered, into the first tabernacle the priests enter at all times, accomplishing the services;
texts.heb.9.7: but into the second, the high priest only, once a year, not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the errors of the people:
texts.heb.9.8: the Holy Spirit shewing this, that the way of the [holy of] holies has not yet been made manifest while as yet the first tabernacle has [its] standing;
texts.heb.9.9: the which [is] an image for the present time, according to which both gifts and sacrifices, unable to perfect as to conscience him that worshipped, are offered,
texts.heb.9.10: [consisting] only of meats and drinks and divers washings, ordinances of flesh, imposed until [the] time of setting things right.
texts.heb.9.11: But Christ being come high priest of the good things to come, by the better and more perfect tabernacle not made with hand, (that is, not of this creation,)
texts.heb.9.12: nor by blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood, has entered in once for all into the [holy of] holies, having found an eternal redemption.
texts.heb.9.13: For if the blood of goats and bulls, and a heifer's ashes sprinkling the defiled, sanctifies for the purity of the flesh,
texts.heb.9.14: how much rather shall the blood of the Christ, who by the eternal Spirit offered himself spotless to God, purify your conscience from dead works to worship [the] living God?
texts.heb.9.15: And for this reason he is mediator of a new covenant, so that, death having taken place for redemption of the transgressions under the first covenant, the called might receive the promise of the eternal inheritance.
texts.heb.9.16: (For where [there is] a testament, the death of the testator must needs come in.
texts.heb.9.17: For a testament [is] of force when men are dead, since it is in no way of force while the testator is alive.)
texts.heb.9.18: Whence neither the first was inaugurated without blood.
texts.heb.9.19: For every commandment having been spoken according to [the] law by Moses to all the people; having taken the blood of calves and goats, with water and scarlet wool and hyssop, he sprinkled both the book itself and all the people,
texts.heb.9.20: saying, This [is] the blood of the covenant which God has enjoined to you.
texts.heb.9.21: And the tabernacle too and all the vessels of service he sprinkled in like manner with blood;
texts.heb.9.22: and almost all things are purified with blood according to the law, and without blood-shedding there is no remission.
texts.heb.9.23: [It was] necessary then that the figurative representations of the things in the heavens should be purified with these; but the heavenly things themselves with sacrifices better than these.
texts.heb.9.24: For the Christ is not entered into holy places made with hand, figures of the true, but into heaven itself, now to appear before the face of God for us:
texts.heb.9.25: nor in order that he should offer himself often, as the high priest enters into the holy places every year with blood not his own;
texts.heb.9.26: since he had [then] been obliged often to suffer from the foundation of the world. But now once in the consummation of the ages he has been manifested for [the] putting away of sin by his sacrifice.
texts.heb.9.27: And forasmuch as it is the portion of men once to die, and after this judgment;
texts.heb.9.28: thus the Christ also, having been once offered to bear the sins of many, shall appear to those that look for him the second time without sin for salvation.
texts.heb.10.1: For the law, having a shadow of the coming good things, not the image itself of the things, can never, by the same sacrifices which they offer continually yearly, perfect those who approach.
texts.heb.10.2: Since, would they not indeed have ceased being offered, on account of the worshippers once purged having no longer any conscience of sins?
texts.heb.10.3: But in these [there is] a calling to mind of sins yearly.
texts.heb.10.4: For blood of bulls and goats [is] incapable of taking away sins.
texts.heb.10.5: Wherefore coming into the world he says, Sacrifice and offering thou willedst not; but thou hast prepared me a body.
texts.heb.10.6: Thou tookest no pleasure in burnt-offerings and sacrifices for sin.
texts.heb.10.7: Then I said, Lo, I come (in [the] roll of the book it is written of me) to do, O God, thy will.
texts.heb.10.8: Above, saying Sacrifices and offerings and burnt-offerings and sacrifices for sin thou willedst not, neither tookest pleasure in (which are offered according to the law);
texts.heb.10.9: then he said, Lo, I come to do thy will. He takes away the first that he may establish the second;
texts.heb.10.10: by which will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
texts.heb.10.11: And every priest stands daily ministering, and offering often the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins.
texts.heb.10.12: But *he*, having offered one sacrifice for sins, sat down in perpetuity at [the] right hand of God,
texts.heb.10.13: waiting from henceforth until his enemies be set [for the] footstool of his feet.
texts.heb.10.14: For by one offering he has perfected in perpetuity the sanctified.
texts.heb.10.15: And the Holy Spirit also bears us witness [of it]; for after what was said:
texts.heb.10.16: This [is] the covenant which I will establish towards them after those days, saith [the] Lord: Giving my laws into their hearts, I will write them also in their understandings;
texts.heb.10.17: and their sins and their lawlessnesses I will never remember any more.
texts.heb.10.18: But where there [is] remission of these, [there is] no longer a sacrifice for sin.
texts.heb.10.19: Having therefore, brethren, boldness for entering into the [holy of] holies by the blood of Jesus,
texts.heb.10.20: the new and living way which he has dedicated for us through the veil, that is, his flesh,
texts.heb.10.21: and [having] a great priest over the house of God,
texts.heb.10.22: let us approach with a true heart, in full assurance of faith, sprinkled as to our hearts from a wicked conscience, and washed as to our body with pure water.
texts.heb.10.23: Let us hold fast the confession of the hope unwavering, (for he [is] faithful who has promised;)
texts.heb.10.24: and let us consider one another for provoking to love and good works;
texts.heb.10.25: not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the custom [is] with some; but encouraging [one another], and by so much the more as ye see the day drawing near.
texts.heb.10.26: For where we sin wilfully after receiving the knowledge of the truth, there no longer remains any sacrifice for sins,
texts.heb.10.27: but a certain fearful expectation of judgment, and heat of fire about to devour the adversaries.
texts.heb.10.28: Any one that has disregarded Moses' law dies without mercy on [the testimony of] two or three witnesses:
texts.heb.10.29: of how much worse punishment, think ye, shall he be judged worthy who has trodden under foot the Son of God, and esteemed the blood of the covenant, whereby he has been sanctified, common, and has insulted the Spirit of grace?
texts.heb.10.30: For we know him that said, To me [belongs] vengeance; *I* will recompense, saith the Lord: and again, The Lord shall judge his people.
texts.heb.10.31: [It is] a fearful thing falling into [the] hands of [the] living God.
texts.heb.10.32: But call to mind the earlier days in which, having been enlightened, ye endured much conflict of sufferings;
texts.heb.10.33: on the one hand, when ye were made a spectacle both in reproaches and afflictions; and on the other, when ye became partakers with those who were passing through them.
texts.heb.10.34: For ye both sympathised with prisoners and accepted with joy the plunder of your goods, knowing that ye have for yourselves a better substance, and an abiding one.
texts.heb.10.35: Cast not away therefore your confidence, which has great recompense.
texts.heb.10.36: For ye have need of endurance in order that, having done the will of God, ye may receive the promise.
texts.heb.10.37: For yet a very little while he that comes will come, and will not delay.
