texts.heb.10.38: But the just shall live by faith; and, if he draw back, my soul does not take pleasure in him.
texts.heb.10.39: But *we* are not drawers back to perdition, but of faith to saving [the] soul.
texts.heb.11.1: Now faith is [the] substantiating of things hoped for, [the] conviction of things not seen.
texts.heb.11.2: For in [the power of] this the elders have obtained testimony.
texts.heb.11.3: By faith we apprehend that the worlds were framed by [the] word of God, so that that which is seen should not take its origin from things which appear.
texts.heb.11.4: By faith Abel offered to God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained testimony of being righteous, God bearing testimony to his gifts, and by it, having died, he yet speaks.
texts.heb.11.5: By faith Enoch was translated that he should not see death; and was not found, because God had translated him; for before [his] translation he has the testimony that he had pleased God.
texts.heb.11.6: But without faith [it is] impossible to please [him]. For he that draws near to God must believe that he is, and [that] he is a rewarder of them who seek him out.
texts.heb.11.7: By faith, Noah, oracularly warned concerning things not yet seen, moved with fear, prepared an ark for the saving of his house; by which he condemned the world, and became heir of the righteousness which [is] according to faith.
texts.heb.11.8: By faith Abraham, being called, obeyed to go out into the place which he was to receive for an inheritance, and went out, not knowing where he was going.
texts.heb.11.9: By faith he sojourned as a stranger in the land of promise as a foreign country, having dwelt in tents with Isaac and Jacob, the heirs with [him] of the same promise;
texts.heb.11.10: for he waited for the city which has foundations, of which God is [the] artificer and constructor.
texts.heb.11.11: By faith also Sarah herself received strength for [the] conception of seed, and [that] beyond a seasonable age; since she counted him faithful who promised.
texts.heb.11.12: Wherefore also there have been born of one, and that of one become dead, even as the stars of heaven in multitude, and as the countless sand which [is] by the sea shore.
texts.heb.11.13: All these died in faith, not having received the promises, but having seen them from afar off and embraced [them], and confessed that they were strangers and sojourners on the earth.
texts.heb.11.14: For they who say such things shew clearly that they seek [their] country.
texts.heb.11.15: And if they had called to mind that from whence they went out, they had had opportunity to have returned;
texts.heb.11.16: but now they seek a better, that is, a heavenly; wherefore God is not ashamed of them, to be called their God; for he has prepared for them a city.
texts.heb.11.17: By faith Abraham, [when] tried, offered up Isaac, and he who had received to himself the promises offered up his only begotten [son],
texts.heb.11.18: as to whom it had been said, In Isaac shall thy seed be called:
texts.heb.11.19: counting that God [was] able to raise [him] even from among [the] dead, whence also he received him in a figure.
texts.heb.11.20: By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau concerning things to come.
texts.heb.11.21: By faith Jacob [when] dying blessed each of the sons of Joseph, and worshipped on the top of his staff.
texts.heb.11.22: By faith Joseph [when] dying called to mind the going forth of the sons of Israel, and gave commandment concerning his bones.
texts.heb.11.23: By faith Moses, being born, was hid three months by his parents, because they saw the child beautiful; and they did not fear the injunction of the king.
texts.heb.11.24: By faith Moses, when he had become great, refused to be called son of Pharaoh's daughter;
texts.heb.11.25: choosing rather to suffer affliction along with the people of God than to have [the] temporary pleasure of sin;
texts.heb.11.26: esteeming the reproach of the Christ greater riches than the treasures of Egypt, for he had respect to the recompense.
texts.heb.11.27: By faith he left Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king; for he persevered, as seeing him who is invisible.
texts.heb.11.28: By faith he celebrated the passover and the sprinkling of the blood, that the destroyer of the firstborn might not touch them.
texts.heb.11.29: By faith they passed through the Red sea as through dry land; of which the Egyptians having made trial were swallowed up.
texts.heb.11.30: By faith the walls of Jericho fell, having been encircled for seven days.
texts.heb.11.31: By faith Rahab the harlot did not perish along with the unbelieving, having received the spies in peace.
texts.heb.11.32: And what more do I say? For the time would fail me telling of Gideon, and Barak, and Samson, and Jephthah, and David and Samuel, and of the prophets:
texts.heb.11.33: who by faith overcame kingdoms, wrought righteousness, obtained promises, stopped lions' mouths,
texts.heb.11.34: quenched [the] power of fire, escaped [the] edge of the sword, became strong out of weakness, became mighty in war, made [the] armies of strangers give way.
texts.heb.11.35: Women received their dead again by resurrection; and others were tortured, not having accepted deliverance, that they might get a better resurrection;
texts.heb.11.36: and others underwent trial of mockings and scourgings, yea, and of bonds and imprisonment.
texts.heb.11.37: They were stoned, were sawn asunder, were tempted, died by the death of the sword; they went about in sheepskins, in goatskins, destitute, afflicted, evil treated,
texts.heb.11.38: (of whom the world was not worthy,) wandering in deserts and mountains, and [in] dens and caverns of the earth.
texts.heb.11.39: And these all, having obtained witness through faith, did not receive the promise,
texts.heb.11.40: God having foreseen some better thing for us, that they should not be made perfect without us.
texts.heb.12.1: Let *us* also therefore, having so great a cloud of witnesses surrounding us, laying aside every weight, and sin which so easily entangles us, run with endurance the race that lies before us,
texts.heb.12.2: looking stedfastly on Jesus the leader and completer of faith: who, in view of the joy lying before him, endured [the] cross, having despised [the] shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God.
texts.heb.12.3: For consider well him who endured so great contradiction from sinners against himself, that ye be not weary, fainting in your minds.
texts.heb.12.4: Ye have not yet resisted unto blood, wrestling against sin.
texts.heb.12.5: And ye have quite forgotten the exhortation which speaks to you as to sons: My son, despise not [the] chastening of [the] Lord, nor faint [when] reproved by him;
texts.heb.12.6: for whom [the] Lord loves he chastens, and scourges every son whom he receives.
texts.heb.12.7: Ye endure for chastening, God conducts himself towards you as towards sons; for who is the son that the father chastens not?
texts.heb.12.8: But if ye are without chastening, of which all have been made partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons.
texts.heb.12.9: Moreover we have had the fathers of our flesh as chasteners, and we reverenced [them]; shall we not much rather be in subjection to the Father of spirits, and live?
texts.heb.12.10: For they indeed chastened for a few days, as seemed good to them; but he for profit, in order to the partaking of his holiness.
texts.heb.12.11: But no chastening at the time seems to be [matter] of joy, but of grief; but afterwards yields [the] peaceful fruit of righteousness to those exercised by it.
texts.heb.12.12: Wherefore lift up the hands that hang down, and the failing knees;
texts.heb.12.13: and make straight paths for your feet, that that which is lame be not turned aside; but that rather it may be healed.
texts.heb.12.14: Pursue peace with all, and holiness, without which no one shall see the Lord:
texts.heb.12.15: watching lest [there be] any one who lacks the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble [you], and many be defiled by it;
texts.heb.12.16: lest [there be] any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one meal sold his birthright;
texts.heb.12.17: for ye know that also afterwards, desiring to inherit the blessing, he was rejected, (for he found no place for repentance) although he sought it earnestly with tears.
texts.heb.12.18: For ye have not come to [the mount] that might be touched and was all on fire, and to obscurity, and darkness, and tempest,
texts.heb.12.19: and trumpet's sound, and voice of words; which they that heard, excusing themselves, declined [the] word being addressed to them any more:
texts.heb.12.20: (for they were not able to bear what was enjoined: And if a beast should touch the mountain, it shall be stoned;
texts.heb.12.21: and, so fearful was the sight, Moses said, I am exceedingly afraid and full of trembling;)
texts.heb.12.22: but ye have come to mount Zion; and to [the] city of [the] living God, heavenly Jerusalem; and to myriads of angels,
texts.heb.12.23: the universal gathering; and to [the] assembly of the firstborn [who are] registered in heaven; and to God, judge of all; and to [the] spirits of just [men] made perfect;
texts.heb.12.24: and to Jesus, mediator of a new covenant; and to [the] blood of sprinkling, speaking better than Abel.
texts.heb.12.25: See that ye refuse not him that speaks. For if those did not escape who had refused him who uttered the oracles on earth, much more we who turn away from him [who does so] from heaven:
texts.heb.12.26: whose voice then shook the earth; but now he has promised, saying, Yet once will *I* shake not only the earth, but also the heaven.
texts.heb.12.27: But this Yet once, signifies the removing of what is shaken, as being made, that what is not shaken may remain.
texts.heb.12.28: Wherefore let us, receiving a kingdom not to be shaken, have grace, by which let us serve God acceptably with reverence and fear.
texts.heb.12.29: For also our God [is] a consuming fire.
texts.heb.13.2: Be not forgetful of hospitality; for by it some have unawares entertained angels.
texts.heb.13.3: Remember prisoners, as bound with [them]; those that are evil-treated, as being yourselves also in [the] body.
texts.heb.13.4: [Let] marriage [be held] every way in honour, and the bed [be] undefiled; for fornicators and adulterers will God judge.
texts.heb.13.5: [Let your] conversation [be] without love of money, satisfied with [your] present circumstances; for *he* has said, I will not leave thee, neither will I forsake thee.
texts.heb.13.6: So that, taking courage, we may say, The Lord [is] my helper, and I will not be afraid: what will man do unto me?
texts.heb.13.7: Remember your leaders who have spoken to you the word of God; and considering the issue of their conversation, imitate their faith.
texts.heb.13.8: Jesus Christ [is] the same yesterday, and to-day, and to the ages [to come].
texts.heb.13.9: Be not carried away with various and strange doctrines; for [it is] good that the heart be confirmed with grace, not meats; those who have walked in which have not been profited by [them].
texts.heb.13.10: We have an altar of which they have no right to eat who serve the tabernacle;
texts.heb.13.11: for of those beasts whose blood is carried [as sacrifices for sin] into the [holy of] holies by the high priest, of these the bodies are burned outside the camp.
texts.heb.13.12: Wherefore also Jesus, that he might sanctify the people by his own blood, suffered without the gate:
texts.heb.13.13: therefore let us go forth to him without the camp, bearing his reproach:
texts.heb.13.14: for we have not here an abiding city, but we seek the coming one.
texts.heb.13.15: By him therefore let us offer [the] sacrifice of praise continually to God, that is, [the] fruit of [the] lips confessing his name.
texts.heb.13.16: But of doing good and communicating [of your substance] be not forgetful, for with such sacrifices God is well pleased.
texts.heb.13.17: Obey your leaders, and be submissive; for *they* watch over your souls as those that shall give account; that they may do this with joy, and not groaning, for this [would be] unprofitable for you.
texts.heb.13.18: Pray for us: for we persuade ourselves that we have a good conscience, in all things desirous to walk rightly.
texts.heb.13.19: But I much more beseech [you] to do this, that I may the more quickly be restored to you.
texts.heb.13.20: But the God of peace, who brought again from among [the] dead our Lord Jesus, the great shepherd of the sheep, in [the power of the] blood of [the] eternal covenant,
texts.heb.13.21: perfect you in every good work to the doing of his will, doing in you what is pleasing before him through Jesus Christ; to whom [be] glory for the ages of ages. Amen.
texts.heb.13.22: But I beseech you, brethren, bear the word of exhortation, for it is but in few words that I have written to you.
texts.heb.13.23: Know that our brother Timotheus is set at liberty; with whom, if he should come soon, I will see you.
texts.heb.13.24: Salute all your leaders, and all the saints. They from Italy salute you.

texts.heb.1.1: In many parts, and many ways, God of old having spoken to the fathers in the prophets,
texts.heb.1.2: in these last days did speak to us in a Son, whom He appointed heir of all things, through whom also He did make the ages;
texts.heb.1.3: who being the brightness of the glory, and the impress of His subsistence, bearing up also the all things by the saying of his might -- through himself having made a cleansing of our sins, sat down at the right hand of the greatness in the highest,
texts.heb.1.4: having become so much better than the messengers, as he did inherit a more excellent name than they.
texts.heb.1.5: For to which of the messengers said He ever, `My Son thou art -- I to-day have begotten thee?' and again, `I will be to him for a father, and he shall be to Me for a son?'
texts.heb.1.6: and when again He may bring in the first-born to the world, He saith, `And let them bow before him -- all messengers of God;'
texts.heb.1.7: and unto the messengers, indeed, He saith, `Who is making His messengers spirits, and His ministers a flame of fire;'
texts.heb.1.8: and unto the Son: `Thy throne, O God, [is] to the age of the age; a scepter of righteousness [is] the scepter of thy reign;
texts.heb.1.9: thou didst love righteousness, and didst hate lawlessness; because of this did He anoint thee -- God, thy God -- with oil of gladness above thy partners;'
texts.heb.1.10: and, `Thou, at the beginning, Lord, the earth didst found, and a work of thy hands are the heavens;
texts.heb.1.11: these shall perish, and Thou dost remain, and all, as a garment, shall become old,
texts.heb.1.12: and as a mantle Thou shall roll them together, and they shall be changed, and Thou art the same, and Thy years shall not fail.'
texts.heb.1.13: And unto which of the messengers said He ever, `Sit at My right hand, till I may make thine enemies thy footstool?'
texts.heb.1.14: are they not all spirits of service -- for ministration being sent forth because of those about to inherit salvation?
texts.heb.2.1: Because of this it behoveth [us] more abundantly to take heed to the things heard, lest we may glide aside,
texts.heb.2.2: for if the word being spoken through messengers did become stedfast, and every transgression and disobedience did receive a just recompense,
texts.heb.2.3: how shall we escape, having neglected so great salvation? which a beginning receiving -- to be spoken through the Lord -- by those having heard was confirmed to us,
texts.heb.2.4: God also bearing joint-witness both with signs and wonders, and manifold powers, and distributions of the Holy Spirit, according to His will.
texts.heb.2.5: For not to messengers did He subject the coming world, concerning which we speak,
texts.heb.2.6: and one in a certain place did testify fully, saying, `What is man, that Thou art mindful of him, or a son of man, that Thou dost look after him?
texts.heb.2.7: Thou didst make him some little less than messengers, with glory and honour Thou didst crown him, and didst set him over the works of Thy hands,
texts.heb.2.8: all things Thou didst put in subjection under his feet,' for in the subjecting to him the all things, nothing did He leave to him unsubjected, and now not yet do we see the all things subjected to him,
texts.heb.2.9: and him who was made some little less than messengers we see -- Jesus -- because of the suffering of the death, with glory and honour having been crowned, that by the grace of God for every one he might taste of death.
texts.heb.2.10: For it was becoming to Him, because of whom [are] the all things, and through whom [are] the all things, many sons to glory bringing, the author of their salvation through sufferings to make perfect,
texts.heb.2.11: for both he who is sanctifying and those sanctified [are] all of one, for which cause he is not ashamed to call them brethren,
texts.heb.2.12: saying, `I will declare Thy name to my brethren, in the midst of an assembly I will sing praise to Thee;' and again, `I will be trusting on Him;'
texts.heb.2.13: and again, `Behold I and the children that God did give to me.'
texts.heb.2.14: Seeing, then, the children have partaken of flesh and blood, he himself also in like manner did take part of the same, that through death he might destroy him having the power of death -- that is, the devil --
texts.heb.2.15: and might deliver those, whoever, with fear of death, throughout all their life, were subjects of bondage,
texts.heb.2.16: for, doubtless, of messengers it doth not lay hold, but of seed of Abraham it layeth hold,
texts.heb.2.17: wherefore it did behove him in all things to be made like to the brethren, that he might become a kind and stedfast chief-priest in the things with God, to make propitiation for the sins of the people,
texts.heb.2.18: for in that he suffered, himself being tempted, he is able to help those who are tempted.
texts.heb.3.1: Wherefore, holy brethren, partakers of a heavenly calling, consider the apostle and chief priest of our profession, Christ Jesus,
texts.heb.3.2: being stedfast to Him who did appoint him, as also Moses in all his house,
texts.heb.3.3: for of more glory than Moses hath this one been counted worthy, inasmuch as more honour than the house hath he who doth build it,
texts.heb.3.4: for every house is builded by some one, and He who the all things did build [is] God,
texts.heb.3.5: and Moses indeed [was] stedfast in all his house, as an attendant, for a testimony of those things that were to be spoken,
texts.heb.3.6: and Christ, as a Son over his house, whose house are we, if the boldness and the rejoicing of the hope unto the end we hold fast.
texts.heb.3.7: Wherefore, (as the Holy Spirit saith, `To-day, if His voice ye may hear --
texts.heb.3.8: ye may not harden your hearts, as in the provocation, in the day of the temptation in the wilderness,
texts.heb.3.9: in which tempt Me did your fathers, they did prove Me, and saw My works forty years;
texts.heb.3.10: wherefore I was grieved with that generation, and said, Always do they go astray in heart, and these have not known My ways;
texts.heb.3.11: so I sware in My anger, If they shall enter into My rest -- !')
texts.heb.3.12: See, brethren, lest there shall be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief in the falling away from the living God,
texts.heb.3.13: but exhort ye one another every day, while the To-day is called, that none of you may be hardened by the deceitfulness of the sin,
texts.heb.3.14: for partakers we have become of the Christ, if the beginning of the confidence unto the end we may hold fast,
texts.heb.3.15: in its being said, `To-day, if His voice ye may hear, ye may not harden your hearts, as in the provocation,'
texts.heb.3.16: for certain having heard did provoke, but not all who did come out of Egypt through Moses;
texts.heb.3.17: but with whom was He grieved forty years? was it not with those who did sin, whose carcasses fell in the wilderness?
texts.heb.3.18: and to whom did He swear that they shall not enter into His rest, except to those who did not believe? --
texts.heb.3.19: and we see that they were not able to enter in because of unbelief.
texts.heb.4.1: We may fear, then, lest a promise being left of entering into His rest, any one of you may seem to have come short,
texts.heb.4.2: for we also are having good news proclaimed, even as they, but the word heard did not profit them, not being mixed with faith in those who heard,
texts.heb.4.3: for we do enter into the rest -- we who did believe, as He said, `So I sware in My anger, If they shall enter into My rest -- ;' and yet the works were done from the foundation of the world,
texts.heb.4.4: for He spake in a certain place concerning the seventh [day] thus: `And God did rest in the seventh day from all His works;'
texts.heb.4.5: and in this [place] again, `If they shall enter into My rest -- ;'
texts.heb.4.6: since then, it remaineth for certain to enter into it, and those who did first hear good news entered not in because of unbelief --
texts.heb.4.7: again He doth limit a certain day, `To-day,' (in David saying, after so long a time,) as it hath been said, `To-day, if His voice ye may hear, ye may not harden your hearts,'
texts.heb.4.8: for if Joshua had given them rest, He would not concerning another day have spoken after these things;
texts.heb.4.9: there doth remain, then, a sabbatic rest to the people of God,
texts.heb.4.10: for he who did enter into his rest, he also rested from his works, as God from His own.
texts.heb.4.11: May we be diligent, then, to enter into that rest, that no one in the same example of the unbelief may fall,
texts.heb.4.12: for the reckoning of God is living, and working, and sharp above every two-edged sword, and piercing unto the dividing asunder both of soul and spirit, of joints also and marrow, and a discerner of thoughts and intents of the heart;
texts.heb.4.13: and there is not a created thing not manifest before Him, but all things [are] naked and open to His eyes -- with whom is our reckoning.
texts.heb.4.14: Having, then, a great chief priest passed through the heavens -- Jesus the Son of God -- may we hold fast the profession,
texts.heb.4.15: for we have not a chief priest unable to sympathise with our infirmities, but [one] tempted in all things in like manner -- apart from sin;
texts.heb.4.16: we may come near, then, with freedom, to the throne of the grace, that we may receive kindness, and find grace -- for seasonable help.
texts.heb.5.1: For every chief priest -- out of men taken -- in behalf of men is set in things [pertaining] to God, that he may offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins,
texts.heb.5.2: able to be gentle to those ignorant and going astray, since himself also is compassed with infirmity;
texts.heb.5.3: and because of this infirmity he ought, as for the people, so also for himself to offer for sins;
texts.heb.5.4: and no one to himself doth take the honour, but he who is called by God, as also Aaron:
texts.heb.5.5: so also the Christ did not glorify himself to become chief priest, but He who spake unto him: `My Son thou art, I to-day have begotten thee;'
texts.heb.5.6: as also in another [place] He saith, `Thou [art] a priest -- to the age, according to the order of Melchisedek;'
texts.heb.5.7: who in the days of his flesh both prayers and supplications unto Him who was able to save him from death -- with strong crying and tears -- having offered up, and having been heard in respect to that which he feared,
texts.heb.5.8: through being a Son, did learn by the things which he suffered -- the obedience,
texts.heb.5.9: and having been made perfect, he did become to all those obeying him a cause of salvation age-during,
texts.heb.5.10: having been addressed by God a chief priest, according to the order of Melchisedek,
texts.heb.5.11: concerning whom we have much discourse and of hard explanation to say, since ye have become dull of hearing,
texts.heb.5.12: for even owing to be teachers, because of the time, again ye have need that one teach you what [are] the elements of the beginning of the oracles of God, and ye have become having need of milk, and not of strong food,
texts.heb.5.13: for every one who is partaking of milk [is] unskilled in the word of righteousness -- for he is an infant,
texts.heb.5.14: and of perfect men is the strong food, who because of the use are having the senses exercised, unto the discernment both of good and of evil.
texts.heb.6.1: Wherefore, having left the word of the beginning of the Christ, unto the perfection we may advance, not again a foundation laying of reformation from dead works, and of faith on God,
texts.heb.6.2: of the teaching of baptisms, of laying on also of hands, of rising again also of the dead, and of judgment age-during,
texts.heb.6.3: and this we will do, if God may permit,
texts.heb.6.4: for [it is] impossible for those once enlightened, having tasted also of the heavenly gift, and partakers having became of the Holy Spirit,
texts.heb.6.5: and did taste the good saying of God, the powers also of the coming age,
texts.heb.6.6: and having fallen away, again to renew [them] to reformation, having crucified again to themselves the Son of God, and exposed to public shame.
texts.heb.6.7: For earth, that is drinking in the rain many times coming upon it, and is bringing forth herbs fit for those because of whom also it is dressed, doth partake of blessing from God,
texts.heb.6.8: and that which is bearing thorns and briers [is] disapproved of, and nigh to cursing, whose end [is] for burning;
texts.heb.6.9: and we are persuaded, concerning you, beloved, the things that are better, and accompanying salvation, though even thus we speak,
texts.heb.6.10: for God is not unrighteous to forget your work, and the labour of the love, that ye shewed to His name, having ministered to the saints and ministering;
texts.heb.6.11: and we desire each one of you the same diligence to shew, unto the full assurance of the hope unto the end,
texts.heb.6.12: that ye may not become slothful, but followers of those who through faith and patient endurance are inheriting the promises.
texts.heb.6.13: For to Abraham God, having made promise, seeing He was able to swear by no greater, did swear by Himself,
texts.heb.6.14: saying, `Blessing indeed I will bless thee, and multiplying I will multiply thee;'
texts.heb.6.15: and so, having patiently endured, he did obtain the promise;
texts.heb.6.16: for men indeed do swear by the greater, and an end of all controversy to them for confirmation [is] the oath,
texts.heb.6.17: in which God, more abundantly willing to shew to the heirs of the promise the immutability of his counsel, did interpose by an oath,
texts.heb.6.18: that through two immutable things, in which [it is] impossible for God to lie, a strong comfort we may have who did flee for refuge to lay hold on the hope set before [us],
texts.heb.6.19: which we have, as an anchor of the soul, both sure and stedfast, and entering into that within the vail,
texts.heb.6.20: whither a forerunner for us did enter -- Jesus, after the order of Melchisedek chief priest having become -- to the age.
texts.heb.7.1: For this Melchisedek, king of Salem, priest of God Most High, who did meet Abraham turning back from the smiting of the kings, and did bless him,
texts.heb.7.2: to whom also a tenth of all did Abraham divide, (first, indeed, being interpreted, `King of righteousness,' and then also, King of Salem, which is, King of Peace,)
texts.heb.7.3: without father, without mother, without genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, and being made like to the Son of God, doth remain a priest continually.
texts.heb.7.4: And see how great this one [is], to whom also a tenth Abraham the patriarch did give out of the best of the spoils,
texts.heb.7.5: and those, indeed, out of the sons of Levi receiving the priesthood, a command have to take tithes from the people according to the law, that is, their brethren, even though they came forth out of the loins of Abraham;
texts.heb.7.6: and he who was not reckoned by genealogy of them, received tithes from Abraham, and him having the promises he hath blessed,
texts.heb.7.7: and apart from all controversy, the less by the better is blessed --
texts.heb.7.8: and here, indeed, men who die do receive tithes, and there [he], who is testified to that he was living,
texts.heb.7.9: and so to speak, through Abraham even Levi who is receiving tithes, hath paid tithes,
texts.heb.7.10: for he was yet in the loins of the father when Melchisedek met him.
texts.heb.7.11: If indeed, then, perfection were through the Levitical priesthood -- for the people under it had received law -- what further need, according to the order of Melchisedek, for another priest to arise, and not to be called according to the order of Aaron?
texts.heb.7.12: for the priesthood being changed, of necessity also, of the law a change doth come,
texts.heb.7.13: for he of whom these things are said in another tribe hath had part, of whom no one gave attendance at the altar,
texts.heb.7.14: for [it is] evident that out of Judah hath arisen our Lord, in regard to which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood.
texts.heb.7.15: And it is yet more abundantly most evident, if according to the similitude of Melchisedek there doth arise another priest,
texts.heb.7.16: who came not according to the law of a fleshly command, but according to the power of an endless life,
texts.heb.7.17: for He doth testify -- `Thou [art] a priest -- to the age, according to the order of Melchisedek;'
texts.heb.7.18: for a disannulling indeed doth come of the command going before because of its weakness, and unprofitableness,
texts.heb.7.19: (for nothing did the law perfect) and the bringing in of a better hope, through which we draw nigh to God.
texts.heb.7.20: And inasmuch as [it is] not apart from oath, (for those indeed apart from oath are become priests,
texts.heb.7.21: and he with an oath through Him who is saying unto him, `The Lord sware, and will not repent, Thou [art] a priest -- to the age, according to the order of Melchisedek;')
texts.heb.7.22: by so much of a better covenant hath Jesus become surety,
texts.heb.7.23: and those indeed are many who have become priests, because by death they are hindered from remaining;
texts.heb.7.24: and he, because of his remaining -- to the age, hath the priesthood not transient,
texts.heb.7.25: whence also he is able to save to the very end, those coming through him unto God -- ever living to make intercession for them.
texts.heb.7.26: For such a chief priest did become us -- kind, harmless, undefiled, separate from the sinners, and become higher than the heavens,
texts.heb.7.27: who hath no necessity daily, as the chief priests, first for his own sins to offer up sacrifice, then for those of the people; for this he did once, having offered up himself;
texts.heb.7.28: for the law doth appoint men chief priests, having infirmity, but the word of the oath that [is] after the law [appointeth] the Son -- to the age having been perfected.
texts.heb.8.1: And the sum concerning the things spoken of [is]: we have such a chief priest, who did sit down at the right hand of the throne of the greatness in the heavens,
texts.heb.8.2: of the holy places a servant, and of the true tabernacle, which the Lord did set up, and not man,
texts.heb.8.3: for every chief priest to offer both gifts and sacrifices is appointed, whence [it is] necessary for this one to have also something that he may offer;
texts.heb.8.4: for if, indeed, he were upon earth, he would not be a priest -- (there being the priests who are offering according to the law, the gifts,
texts.heb.8.5: who unto an example and shadow do serve of the heavenly things, as Moses hath been divinely warned, being about to construct the tabernacle, for `See (saith He) thou mayest make all things according to the pattern that was shewn to thee in the mount;') --
texts.heb.8.6: and now he hath obtained a more excellent service, how much also of a better covenant is he mediator, which on better promises hath been sanctioned,
texts.heb.8.7: for if that first were faultless, a place would not have been sought for a second.
texts.heb.8.8: For finding fault, He saith to them, `Lo, days come, saith the Lord, and I will complete with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah, a new covenant,
texts.heb.8.9: not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers, in the day of My taking [them] by their hand, to bring them out of the land of Egypt -- because they did not remain in My covenant, and I did not regard them, saith the Lord, --
texts.heb.8.10: because this [is] the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel, after those days, saith the Lord, giving My laws into their mind, and upon their hearts I will write them, and I will be to them for a God, and they shall be to Me for a people;
texts.heb.8.11: and they shall not teach each his neighbour, and each his brother, saying, Know thou the Lord, because they shall all know Me from the small one of them unto the great one of them,
texts.heb.8.12: because I will be merciful to their unrighteousness, and their sins and their lawlessnesses I will remember no more;' --
texts.heb.8.13: in the saying `new,' He hath made the first old, and what doth become obsolete and is old [is] nigh disappearing.
texts.heb.9.1: It had, indeed, then (even the first tabernacle) ordinances of service, also a worldly sanctuary,
texts.heb.9.2: for a tabernacle was prepared, the first, in which was both the lamp-stand, and the table, and the bread of the presence -- which is called `Holy;'
texts.heb.9.3: and after the second vail a tabernacle that is called `Holy of holies,'
texts.heb.9.4: having a golden censer, and the ark of the covenant overlaid all round about with gold, in which [is] the golden pot having the manna, and the rod of Aaron that budded, and the tables of the covenant,
texts.heb.9.5: and over it cherubim of the glory, overshadowing the mercy-seat, concerning which we are not now to speak particularly.
texts.heb.9.6: And these things having been thus prepared, into the first tabernacle, indeed, at all times the priests do go in, performing the services,
texts.heb.9.7: and into the second, once in the year, only the chief priest, not apart from blood, which he doth offer for himself and the errors of the people,
texts.heb.9.8: the Holy Spirit this evidencing that not yet hath been manifested the way of the holy [places], the first tabernacle having yet a standing;
texts.heb.9.9: which [is] a simile in regard to the present time, in which both gifts and sacrifices are offered, which are not able, in regard to conscience, to make perfect him who is serving,
texts.heb.9.10: only in victuals, and drinks, and different baptisms, and fleshly ordinances -- till the time of reformation imposed upon [them].
texts.heb.9.11: And Christ being come, chief priest of the coming good things, through the greater and more perfect tabernacle not made with hands -- that is, not of this creation --
texts.heb.9.12: neither through blood of goats and calves, but through his own blood, did enter in once into the holy places, age-during redemption having obtained;
texts.heb.9.13: for if the blood of bulls, and goats, and ashes of an heifer, sprinkling those defiled, doth sanctify to the purifying of the flesh,
texts.heb.9.14: how much more shall the blood of the Christ (who through the age-during Spirit did offer himself unblemished to God) purify your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?
texts.heb.9.15: And because of this, of a new covenant he is mediator, that, death having come, for redemption of the transgressions under the first covenant, those called may receive the promise of the age-during inheritance,
texts.heb.9.16: for where a covenant [is], the death of the covenant-victim to come in is necessary,
texts.heb.9.17: for a covenant over dead victims [is] stedfast, since it is no force at all when the covenant-victim liveth,
texts.heb.9.18: whence not even the first apart from blood hath been initiated,
texts.heb.9.19: for every command having been spoken, according to law, by Moses, to all the people, having taken the blood of the calves and goats, with water, and scarlet wool, and hyssop, he both the book itself and all the people did sprinkle,
texts.heb.9.20: saying, `This [is] the blood of the covenant that God enjoined unto you,'
texts.heb.9.21: and both the tabernacle and all the vessels of the service with blood in like manner he did sprinkle,
texts.heb.9.22: and with blood almost all things are purified according to the law, and apart from blood-shedding forgiveness doth not come.
texts.heb.9.23: [It is] necessary, therefore, the pattern indeed of the things in the heavens to be purified with these, and the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these;
texts.heb.9.24: for not into holy places made with hands did the Christ enter -- figures of the true -- but into the heaven itself, now to be manifested in the presence of God for us;
texts.heb.9.25: nor that he may many times offer himself, even as the chief priest doth enter into the holy places every year with blood of others;
texts.heb.9.26: since it had behoved him many times to suffer from the foundation of the world, but now once, at the full end of the ages, for putting away of sin through his sacrifice, he hath been manifested;
texts.heb.9.27: and as it is laid up to men once to die, and after this -- judgment,
texts.heb.9.28: so also the Christ, once having been offered to bear the sins of many, a second time, apart from a sin-offering, shall appear, to those waiting for him -- to salvation!
texts.heb.10.1: For the law having a shadow of the coming good things -- not the very image of the matters, every year, by the same sacrifices that they offer continually, is never able to make perfect those coming near,
texts.heb.10.2: since, would they not have ceased to be offered, because of those serving having no more conscience of sins, having once been purified?
texts.heb.10.3: but in those [sacrifices] is a remembrance of sins every year,
texts.heb.10.4: for it is impossible for blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.
texts.heb.10.5: Wherefore, coming into the world, he saith, `Sacrifice and offering Thou didst not will, and a body Thou didst prepare for me,
texts.heb.10.6: in burnt-offerings, and concerning sin-offerings, Thou didst not delight,
texts.heb.10.7: then I said, Lo, I come, (in a volume of the book it hath been written concerning me,) to do, O God, Thy will;'
texts.heb.10.8: saying above -- `Sacrifice, and offering, and burnt-offerings, and concerning sin-offering Thou didst not will, nor delight in,' -- which according to the law are offered --
texts.heb.10.9: then he said, `Lo, I come to do, O God, Thy will;' he doth take away the first that the second he may establish;
texts.heb.10.10: in the which will we are having been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once,
texts.heb.10.11: and every priest, indeed, hath stood daily serving, and the same sacrifices many times offering, that are never able to take away sins.
texts.heb.10.12: And He, for sin one sacrifice having offered -- to the end, did sit down on the right hand of God, --
texts.heb.10.13: as to the rest, expecting till He may place his enemies [as] his footstool,
texts.heb.10.14: for by one offering he hath perfected to the end those sanctified;
texts.heb.10.15: and testify to us also doth the Holy Spirit, for after that He hath said before,
texts.heb.10.16: `This [is] the covenant that I will make with them after those days, saith the Lord, giving My laws on their hearts, and upon their minds I will write them,'
texts.heb.10.17: and `their sins and their lawlessness I will remember no more;'
texts.heb.10.18: and where forgiveness of these [is], there is no more offering for sin.
texts.heb.10.19: Having, therefore, brethren, boldness for the entrance into the holy places, in the blood of Jesus,
texts.heb.10.20: which way he did initiate for us -- new and living, through the vail, that is, his flesh --
texts.heb.10.21: and a high priest over the house of God,
texts.heb.10.22: may we draw near with a true heart, in full assurance of faith, having the hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, and having the body bathed with pure water;
texts.heb.10.23: may we hold fast the unwavering profession of the hope, (for faithful [is] He who did promise),
texts.heb.10.24: and may we consider one another to provoke to love and to good works,
texts.heb.10.25: not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as a custom of certain [is], but exhorting, and so much the more as ye see the day coming nigh.
texts.heb.10.26: For we -- willfully sinning after the receiving the full knowledge of the truth -- no more for sins doth there remain a sacrifice,
texts.heb.10.27: but a certain fearful looking for of judgment, and fiery zeal, about to devour the opposers;
texts.heb.10.28: any one who did set at nought a law of Moses, apart from mercies, by two or three witnesses, doth die,
texts.heb.10.29: of how much sorer punishment shall he be counted worthy who the Son of God did trample on, and the blood of the covenant did count a common thing, in which he was sanctified, and to the Spirit of the grace did despite?
texts.heb.10.30: for we have known Him who is saying, `Vengeance [is] Mine, I will recompense, saith the Lord;' and again, `The Lord shall judge His people;' --
texts.heb.10.31: fearful [is] the falling into the hands of a living God.
texts.heb.10.32: And call to your remembrance the former days, in which, having been enlightened, ye did endure much conflict of sufferings,
texts.heb.10.33: partly both with reproaches and tribulations being made spectacles, and partly having become partners of those so living,
texts.heb.10.34: for also with my bonds ye sympathised, and the robbery of your goods with joy ye did receive, knowing that ye have in yourselves a better substance in the heavens, and an enduring one.
texts.heb.10.35: Ye may not cast away, then, your boldness, which hath great recompense of reward,
texts.heb.10.36: for of patience ye have need, that the will of God having done, ye may receive the promise,
texts.heb.10.37: for yet a very very little, He who is coming will come, and will not tarry;
texts.heb.10.38: and `the righteous by faith shall live,' and `if he may draw back, My soul hath no pleasure in him,'
texts.heb.10.39: and we are not of those drawing back to destruction, but of those believing to a preserving of soul.
texts.heb.11.1: And faith is of things hoped for a confidence, of matters not seen a conviction,
texts.heb.11.2: for in this were the elders testified of;
texts.heb.11.3: by faith we understand the ages to have been prepared by a saying of God, in regard to the things seen not having come out of things appearing;
texts.heb.11.4: by faith a better sacrifice did Abel offer to God than Cain, through which he was testified to be righteous, God testifying of his gifts, and through it, he being dead, doth yet speak.
texts.heb.11.5: By faith Enoch was translated -- not to see death, and was not found, because God did translate him; for before his translation he had been testified to -- that he had pleased God well,
texts.heb.11.6: and apart from faith it is impossible to please well, for it behoveth him who is coming to God to believe that He is, and to those seeking Him He becometh a rewarder.
texts.heb.11.7: By faith Noah, having been divinely warned concerning the things not yet seen, having feared, did prepare an ark to the salvation of his house, through which he did condemn the world, and of the righteousness according to faith he became heir.
texts.heb.11.8: By faith Abraham, being called, did obey, to go forth to the place that he was about to receive for an inheritance, and he went forth, not knowing whither he doth go;
texts.heb.11.9: by faith he did sojourn in the land of the promise as a strange country, in tabernacles having dwelt with Isaac and Jacob, fellow-heirs of the same promise,
texts.heb.11.10: for he was looking for the city having the foundations, whose artificer and constructor [is] God.
texts.heb.11.11: By faith also Sarah herself did receive power to conceive seed, and she bare after the time of life, seeing she did judge Him faithful who did promise;
texts.heb.11.12: wherefore, also from one were begotten -- and that of one who had become dead -- as the stars of the heaven in multitude, and as sand that [is] by the sea-shore -- the innumerable.
texts.heb.11.13: In faith died all these, not having received the promises, but from afar having seen them, and having been persuaded, and having saluted [them], and having confessed that strangers and sojourners they are upon the earth,
texts.heb.11.14: for those saying such things make manifest that they seek a country;
texts.heb.11.15: and if, indeed, they had been mindful of that from which they came forth, they might have had an opportunity to return,
texts.heb.11.16: but now they long for a better, that is, an heavenly, wherefore God is not ashamed of them, to be called their God, for He did prepare for them a city.
texts.heb.11.17: By faith Abraham hath offered up Isaac, being tried, and the only begotten he did offer up who did receive the promises,
texts.heb.11.18: of whom it was said -- `In Isaac shall a seed be called to thee;'
texts.heb.11.19: reckoning that even out of the dead God is able to raise up, whence also in a figure he did receive [him].
texts.heb.11.20: By faith, concerning coming things, Isaac did bless Jacob and Esau;
texts.heb.11.21: by faith Jacob dying -- each of the sons of Joseph did bless, and did bow down upon the top of his staff;
texts.heb.11.22: by faith, Joseph dying, concerning the outgoing of the sons of Israel did make mention, and concerning his bones did give command.
texts.heb.11.23: By faith Moses, having been born, was hid three months by his parents, because they saw the child comely, and were not afraid of the decree of the king;
texts.heb.11.24: by faith Moses, having become great, did refuse to be called a son of the daughter of Pharaoh,
texts.heb.11.25: having chosen rather to be afflicted with the people of God, than to have sin's pleasure for a season,
texts.heb.11.26: greater wealth having reckoned the reproach of the Christ than the treasures in Egypt, for he did look to the recompense of reward;
texts.heb.11.27: by faith he left Egypt behind, not having been afraid of the wrath of the king, for, as seeing the Invisible One -- he endured;
texts.heb.11.28: by faith he kept the passover, and the sprinkling of the blood, that He who is destroying the first-born might not touch them.
texts.heb.11.29: By faith they did pass through the Red Sea as through dry land, which the Egyptians having received a trial of, were swallowed up;
texts.heb.11.30: by faith the walls of Jericho did fall, having been surrounded for seven days;
texts.heb.11.31: by faith Rahab the harlot did not perish with those who disbelieved, having received the spies with peace.
texts.heb.11.32: And what shall I yet say? for the time will fail me recounting about Gideon, Barak also, and Samson, and Jephthah, David also, and Samuel, and the prophets,
texts.heb.11.33: who through faith did subdue kingdoms, wrought righteousness, obtained promises, stopped mouths of lions,
texts.heb.11.34: quenched the power of fire, escaped the mouth of the sword, were made powerful out of infirmities, became strong in battle, caused to give way camps of the aliens.
texts.heb.11.35: Women received by a rising again their dead, and others were tortured, not accepting the redemption, that a better rising again they might receive,
texts.heb.11.36: and others of mockings and scourgings did receive trial, and yet of bonds and imprisonment;
texts.heb.11.37: they were stoned, they were sawn asunder, they were tried; in the killing of the sword they died; they went about in sheepskins, in goatskins -- being destitute, afflicted, injuriously treated,
texts.heb.11.38: of whom the world was not worthy; in deserts wandering, and [in] mountains, and [in] caves, and [in] the holes of the earth;
texts.heb.11.39: and these all, having been testified to through the faith, did not receive the promise,
texts.heb.11.40: God for us something better having provided, that apart from us they might not be made perfect.
texts.heb.12.1: Therefore, we also having so great a cloud of witnesses set around us, every weight having put off, and the closely besetting sin, through endurance may we run the contest that is set before us,
texts.heb.12.2: looking to the author and perfecter of faith -- Jesus, who, over-against the joy set before him -- did endure a cross, shame having despised, on the right hand also of the throne of God did sit down;
texts.heb.12.3: for consider again him who endured such gainsaying from the sinners to himself, that ye may not be wearied in your souls -- being faint.
texts.heb.12.4: Not yet unto blood did ye resist -- with the sin striving;
texts.heb.12.5: and ye have forgotten the exhortation that doth speak fully with you as with sons, `My son, be not despising chastening of the Lord, nor be faint, being reproved by Him,
texts.heb.12.6: for whom the Lord doth love He doth chasten, and He scourgeth every son whom He receiveth;'
texts.heb.12.7: if chastening ye endure, as to sons God beareth Himself to you, for who is a son whom a father doth not chasten?
texts.heb.12.8: and if ye are apart from chastening, of which all have become partakers, then bastards are ye, and not sons.
texts.heb.12.9: Then, indeed, fathers of our flesh we have had, chastising [us], and we were reverencing [them]; shall we not much rather be subject to the Father of the spirits, and live?
texts.heb.12.10: for they, indeed, for a few days, according to what seemed good to them, were chastening, but He for profit, to be partakers of His separation;
texts.heb.12.11: and all chastening for the present, indeed, doth not seem to be of joy, but of sorrow, yet afterward the peaceable fruit of righteousness to those exercised through it -- it doth yield.
texts.heb.12.12: Wherefore, the hanging-down hands and the loosened knees set ye up;
texts.heb.12.13: and straight paths make for your feet, that that which is lame may not be turned aside, but rather be healed;
texts.heb.12.14: peace pursue with all, and the separation, apart from which no one shall see the Lord,
texts.heb.12.15: looking diligently over lest any one be failing of the grace of God, lest any root of bitterness springing up may give trouble, and through this many may be defiled;
texts.heb.12.16: lest any one be a fornicator, or a profane person, as Esau, who in exchange for one morsel of food did sell his birthright,
texts.heb.12.17: for ye know that also afterwards, wishing to inherit the blessing, he was disapproved of, for a place of reformation he found not, though with tears having sought it.
texts.heb.12.18: For ye came not near to the mount touched and scorched with fire, and to blackness, and darkness, and tempest,
texts.heb.12.19: and a sound of a trumpet, and a voice of sayings, which those having heard did entreat that a word might not be added to them,
texts.heb.12.20: for they were not bearing that which is commanded, `And if a beast may touch the mountain, it shall be stoned, or with an arrow shot through,'
texts.heb.12.21: and, (so terrible was the sight,) Moses said, `I am fearful exceedingly, and trembling.'
texts.heb.12.22: But, ye came to Mount Zion, and to a city of the living God, to the heavenly Jerusalem, and to myriads of messengers,
texts.heb.12.23: to the company and assembly of the first-born in heaven enrolled, and to God the judge of all, and to spirits of righteous men made perfect,
texts.heb.12.24: and to a mediator of a new covenant -- Jesus, and to blood of sprinkling, speaking better things than that of Abel!
texts.heb.12.25: See, may ye not refuse him who is speaking, for if those did not escape who refused him who upon earth was divinely speaking -- much less we who do turn away from him who [speaketh] from heaven,
texts.heb.12.26: whose voice the earth shook then, and now hath he promised, saying, `Yet once -- I shake not only the earth, but also the heaven;'
texts.heb.12.27: and this -- `Yet once' -- doth make evident the removal of the things shaken, as of things having been made, that the things not shaken may remain;
texts.heb.12.28: wherefore, a kingdom that cannot be shaken receiving, may we have grace, through which we may serve God well-pleasingly, with reverence and religious fear;
texts.heb.12.29: for also our God [is] a consuming fire.
texts.heb.13.2: of the hospitality be not forgetful, for through this unawares certain did entertain messengers;
texts.heb.13.3: be mindful of those in bonds, as having been bound with them, of those maltreated, as also yourselves being in the body;
texts.heb.13.4: honourable [is] the marriage in all, and the bed undefiled, and whoremongers and adulterers God shall judge.
texts.heb.13.5: Without covetousness the behaviour, being content with the things present, for He hath said, `No, I will not leave, no, nor forsake thee,'
texts.heb.13.6: so that we do boldly say, `The Lord [is] to me a helper, and I will not fear what man shall do to me.'
texts.heb.13.7: Be mindful of those leading you, who did speak to you the word of God, whose faith -- considering the issue of the behaviour -- be imitating,
texts.heb.13.8: Jesus Christ yesterday and to-day the same, and to the ages;
texts.heb.13.9: with teachings manifold and strange be not carried about, for [it is] good that by grace the heart be confirmed, not with meats, in which they who were occupied were not profited;
texts.heb.13.10: we have an altar, of which to eat they have no authority who the tabernacle are serving,
texts.heb.13.11: for of those beasts whose blood is brought for sin into the holy places through the chief priest -- of these the bodies are burned without the camp.
texts.heb.13.12: Wherefore, also Jesus -- that he might sanctify through [his] own blood the people -- without the gate did suffer;
texts.heb.13.13: now, then, may we go forth unto him without the camp, his reproach bearing;
texts.heb.13.14: for we have not here an abiding city, but the coming one we seek;
texts.heb.13.15: through him, then, we may offer up a sacrifice of praise always to God, that is, the fruit of lips, giving thanks to His name;
texts.heb.13.16: and of doing good, and of fellowship, be not forgetful, for with such sacrifices God is well-pleased.
texts.heb.13.17: Be obedient to those leading you, and be subject, for these do watch for your souls, as about to give account, that with joy they may do this, and not sighing, for this [is] unprofitable to you.
texts.heb.13.18: Pray for us, for we trust that we have a good conscience, in all things willing to behave well,
texts.heb.13.19: and more abundantly do I call upon [you] to do this, that more quickly I may be restored to you.
texts.heb.13.20: And the God of the peace, who did bring up out of the dead the great shepherd of the sheep -- in the blood of an age-during covenant -- our Lord Jesus,
texts.heb.13.21: make you perfect in every good work to do His will, doing in you that which is well-pleasing before Him, through Jesus Christ, to whom [is] the glory -- to the ages of the ages! Amen.
texts.heb.13.22: And I entreat you, brethren, suffer the word of the exhortation, for also through few words I have written to you.
texts.heb.13.23: Know ye that the brother Timotheus is released, with whom, if he may come more shortly, I will see you.
texts.heb.13.24: Salute all those leading you, and all the saints; salute you doth those from Italy:
texts.heb.13.25: the grace [is] with you all! Amen.

texts.heb.1.1: Dios, que habló muchas veces, y en muchas maneras en otro tiempo a los padres por los profetas,
texts.heb.1.2: Nos ha hablado en estos postreros días por su Hijo, a quien constituyó heredero de todas las cosas, por quien asimismo hizo los siglos;
texts.heb.1.3: El cual siendo el resplandor de su gloria, y la imagen expresa de su sustancia, y sustentando todas las cosas con la palabra de su poder, habiendo hecho la purgación de nuestros pecados por sí mismo, se asentó a la diestra de la majestad en las alturas;
texts.heb.1.4: Siendo hecho tanto más excelente que los ángeles, cuanto alcanzó por herencia más excelente nombre que ellos.
texts.heb.1.5: ¿Porque a cuál de los ángeles dijo Dios jamás: Mi Hijo eres tú, yo te he engendrado hoy? Y otra vez: Yo seré a él Padre, y él me será a mí Hijo?
texts.heb.1.6: Y otra vez, cuando introduce al primogénito en la redondez de la tierra, dice: Y adórenle todos los ángeles de Dios.
texts.heb.1.7: Y ciertamente con respecto a los ángeles dice: El que hace sus ángeles espíritus, y a sus ministros, llama de fuego.
texts.heb.1.8: Mas al Hijo: Tu trono, oh Dios, por los siglos de los siglos: cetro de rectitud el cetro de tu reino.
texts.heb.1.9: Amaste la justicia, y aborreciste la maldad; por esto Dios, tu Dios, te ungió, con el aceite de alegría más que a tus compañeros.
texts.heb.1.10: Y: Tú, Señor, en el principio fundaste la tierra; y los cielos son obras de tus manos:
texts.heb.1.11: Ellos perecerán, mas tú eres permanente; y todos ellos envejecerse han como vestidura;
texts.heb.1.12: Y como un manto los envolverás, y serán mudados: tú empero eres el mismo, y tus años nunca se acabarán.
texts.heb.1.13: Además, ¿a cuál de los ángeles dijo él jamás: Asiéntate a mi diestra, hasta que ponga a tus enemigos por estrado de tus pies?
texts.heb.1.14: ¿No son todos espíritus ministradores, enviados para ministrar por aquellos, que serán herederos de salud?
texts.heb.2.1: Por lo cual es menester que tanto con más diligencia estemos atentos a las cosas que hemos oído, porque no nos escurramos.
texts.heb.2.2: Porque si la palabra dicha por el ministerio de los ángeles fue firme, y toda transgresión y desobediencia recibió justa paga de su galardón,
texts.heb.2.3: ¿Cómo escaparemos nosotros, si tuviéremos en poco una salud tan grande? la cual habiendo primero comenzado a ser publicada por el Señor, ha sido confirmada hasta nosotros por los que le oyeron a él mismo:
texts.heb.2.4: Testificando juntamente con ellos Dios con señales, y maravillas, y con diversos milagros, y dones del Espíritu Santo, repartiéndolos según su voluntad.
texts.heb.2.5: ¶ Porque no sujetó a los ángeles el mundo venidero, del cual hablamos.
texts.heb.2.6: Testificó empero uno en cierto lugar, diciendo: ¿Qué es el hombre que te acuerdas de él, o el hijo del hombre que le visitas?
texts.heb.2.7: Hicístele un poco menor que los ángeles, coronástele de gloria y de honra, y pusístele sobre las obras de tus manos.
texts.heb.2.8: Todas las cosas sujetaste debajo de sus pies. Porque en cuanto le sujetó todas las cosas, nada dejó que no sea sujeto a él. Mas ahora no vemos todavía que todas las cosas le sean sujetas.
texts.heb.2.9: Empero vemos a aquel mismo Jesús, que fue hecho un poco menor que los ángeles por pasión de muerte, coronado de gloria y de honra, para que por la gracia de Dios gustase la muerte por todos.
texts.heb.2.10: Porque convenía, que aquel por cuya causa son todas las cosas, y por el cual son todas las cosas, habiendo de llevar muchos hijos a la gloria, hiciese consumado al príncipe de la salud de ellos por medio de padecimientos.
texts.heb.2.11: Porque el que santifica y los que son santificados de uno son todos; por cuya causa no se avergüenza de llamarlos hermanos,
texts.heb.2.12: Diciendo: Anunciaré tu nombre a mis hermanos, en medio de la iglesia salmearte he.
texts.heb.2.13: Y otra vez: Yo confiaré en él. Y otra vez: He aquí yo, y los hijos que me dio Dios.
texts.heb.2.14: Así que por cuanto los hijos participan de la carne y de la sangre, también él de la misma manera participó de las mismas cosas; para que por medio de la muerte redujese a la impotencia al que tenía la potencia de la muerte, es a saber, al diablo;
texts.heb.2.15: Y librar a los que por el temor de la muerte estaban por toda la vida sujetos a servidumbre.
texts.heb.2.16: Que ciertamente no toma a los ángeles, mas toma a la simiente de Abraham.
texts.heb.2.17: Por lo cual fue necesario que en todo semejase a sus hermanos, para que fuese un sumo sacerdote misericordioso y fiel en lo perteneciente a Dios, a fin de expiar los pecados del pueblo.
texts.heb.2.18: Porque en cuanto él mismo padeció, siendo tentado, es poderoso para también socorrer a los que son tentados.
texts.heb.3.1: Por lo cual hermanos, santos, participantes de la vocación celestial, considerád el apóstol y sumo sacerdote de nuestra profesión Cristo Jesús,
texts.heb.3.2: El cual fue fiel al que le constituyó, como también lo fue Moisés en toda su casa.
texts.heb.3.3: Porque de tanto mayor gloria que Moisés éste es estimado digno, cuanto tiene mayor dignidad que la casa el que la fabricó.
texts.heb.3.4: Porque toda casa es edificada por alguno; mas el que creó todas las cosas, es Dios.
texts.heb.3.5: Y Moisés a la verdad fue fiel en toda su casa, como criado; empero para testificar aquellas cosas que después se habían de denunciar;
texts.heb.3.6: Mas Cristo, como hijo sobre su propia casa, la cual casa somos nosotros, si hasta el cabo retenemos firme la confianza y la alegría de la esperanza.
texts.heb.3.7: Por lo cual, como dice el Espíritu Santo: Si oyereis hoy su voz;
texts.heb.3.8: No endurezcáis vuestros corazones como en la provocación, en el día de la tentación en el desierto,
texts.heb.3.9: Donde me tentaron vuestros padres: me probaron, y vieron mis obras cuarenta años.
texts.heb.3.10: A causa de lo cual me indigné con aquella generación, y dije: Perpetuamente yerran de corazón, y ni ellos han conocido mis caminos;
texts.heb.3.11: Así que juré en mi ira, Si entrarán en mi reposo.
texts.heb.3.12: Estád alerta, hermanos, que en ninguno de vosotros haya corazón maleado de incredulidad para apartarse del Dios vivo;
texts.heb.3.13: Antes exhortáos los unos a los otros cada día, entre tanto que se dice Hoy; porque ninguno de vosotros se endurezca por el engaño del pecado.
texts.heb.3.14: Porque participantes de Cristo somos hechos, si empero retenemos firme hasta el cabo el principio de la confianza.
texts.heb.3.15: Entre tanto que se dice: Si oyereis hoy su voz, no endurezcáis vuestros corazones, como en la provocación.
texts.heb.3.16: Porque algunos, habiendo oído, provocaron; aunque no todos los que salieron de Egipto por medio de Moisés.
texts.heb.3.17: Mas, ¿con quiénes estuvo indignado cuarenta años? ¿no fue con aquellos que pecaron, cuyos miembros cayeron en el desierto?
texts.heb.3.18: ¿Y a quiénes juró que no entrarían en su reposo, sino a aquellos que no creyeron?
texts.heb.3.19: Así vemos que no pudieron entrar a causa de la incredulidad.
texts.heb.4.1: Temamos, pues, no sea que, habiéndo nos sido dejada una promesa de entrada en su reposo, parezca a alguno de nosotros quedar frustrado de ella.
texts.heb.4.2: Porque también a nosotros nos ha sido anunciada la buena nueva como a ellos; mas la palabra oída no les aprovechó a ellos, no siendo mezclada con fe en aquellos que la oyeron.
texts.heb.4.3: Entramos empero en el reposo los que hemos creído, de la manera que dijo: Así que juré en mi ira, si entrarán en mi reposo: aun acabadas las obras desde el principio del mundo.
texts.heb.4.4: Porque en un cierto lugar dijo así del séptimo día: Y reposó Dios de todas sus obras en el séptimo día.
texts.heb.4.5: Y otra vez aquí, Si entrarán en mi reposo.
texts.heb.4.6: Así que pues que resta que algunos han de entrar en él, y que aquellos a quiénes primero fue anunciado el evangelio, no entraron por causa de la incredulidad,
texts.heb.4.7: Determina otra vez un cierto día, diciendo por David: Hoy, tanto tiempo después; como está dicho: Si oyereis hoy su voz, no endurezcáis vuestros corazones.
texts.heb.4.8: Porque si Josué les hubiera dado el reposo, nunca habría él hablado, después de esto, de otro día.
texts.heb.4.9: Así que queda el sabatismo para el pueblo de Dios.
texts.heb.4.10: Porque el que ha entrado en el reposo de él, ha reposado también él mismo de sus propias obras, como Dios reposó de las suyas.
texts.heb.4.11: ¶ Esforcémosnos, pues, a entrar en aquel reposo, a fin de que ninguno caiga en el mismo ejemplo de incredulidad.
texts.heb.4.12: ¶ Porque la palabra de Dios es viva y eficaz, y más penetrante que toda espada de dos filos; y que alcanza hasta partir el alma, y aun el espíritu, y las coyunturas, y tuétanos; y que discierne los pensamientos, y las intenciones del corazón.
texts.heb.4.13: Y no hay criatura alguna que no sea manifiesta en su presencia: antes todas las cosas están desnudas y abiertas a los ojos de aquel a quien tenemos que dar cuenta.
texts.heb.4.14: Teniendo pues un gran sumo sacerdote, que penetró los cielos, Jesús el Hijo de Dios, retengamos firme nuestra profesión.
texts.heb.4.15: Que no tenemos un sumo sacerdote que no se pueda resentir de nuestras flaquezas; mas tentado en todo según nuestra semejanza, sacado el pecado.
texts.heb.4.16: Lleguémosnos, pues, confiadamente al trono de su gracia, a fin de alcanzar misericordia, y hallar gracia para el auxilio oportuno.
texts.heb.5.1: Porque todo sumo sacerdote tomado de entre los hombres, es constituido en favor de los hombres en lo que a Dios toca, para que ofrezca presentes, y también sacrificios por los pecados:
texts.heb.5.2: Que se pueda compadecer de los ignorantes y de los errados, porque él también está rodeado de flaqueza:
texts.heb.5.3: Por causa de la cual deba, como por el pueblo así también por sí mismo, ofrecer sacrificios por los pecados.
texts.heb.5.4: ¶ Ni nadie toma para sí mismo esta honra, sino el que es llamado de Dios, como lo fue Aarón.
texts.heb.5.5: Así también Cristo no se glorificó a sí mismo, para ser hecho sumo sacerdote, sino el que le dijo: Tú eres mi Hijo, yo te he engendrado hoy.
texts.heb.5.6: Como también dice en otro lugar: Tú eres sacerdote eternamente, según el orden de Melquisedec.
texts.heb.5.7: El cual en los días de su carne, habiendo ofrecido ruegos y también suplicaciones con gran clamor y lágrimas a aquel que le podía librar de la muerte, fue oído y librado de su miedo.
texts.heb.5.8: Y aunque era Hijo, sin embargo por lo que padeció aprendió la obediencia;
texts.heb.5.9: Y consumado, fue hecho causa de eterna salud para todos los que le obedecen:
texts.heb.5.10: Nombrado de Dios sumo sacerdote según el orden de Melquisedec.
texts.heb.5.11: ¶ Del cual tenemos mucho que decir, y dificultoso de declarar, por cuanto sois perezosos para oír.
texts.heb.5.12: Porque debiendo de ser ya maestros, a causa del tiempo, tenéis necesidad de volver a ser enseñados, de cuáles sean los elementos del principio de los oráculos de Dios, y sois hechos tales que tengáis necesidad de leche, y no de mantenimiento firme.
texts.heb.5.13: Que cualquiera que usa de leche, no tiene aun experiencia de la palabra de justicia, porque es niño.
texts.heb.5.14: Mas de los ya hombres perfectos es la vianda firme, es a saber, de los que por la costumbre tienen ya los sentidos ejercitados a la discreción del bien y del mal.
texts.heb.6.1: Por lo cual dejando ya la palabra del comienzo en la institución de Cristo, vayamos adelante a la perfección, no echando otra vez el fundamento del arrepentimiento de las obras muertas, y de la fe a Dios,
texts.heb.6.2: De la doctrina de los bautismos, y de la imposición de manos, y de la resurrección de los muertos, y del juicio eterno;
texts.heb.6.3: Y esto haremos, a la verdad, si Dios lo permitiere.
texts.heb.6.4: Porque es imposible que los que una vez recibieron la luz, y que gustaron el don celestial, y que fueron hechos partícipes del Espíritu Santo,
texts.heb.6.5: Y que asimismo gustaron la buena palabra de Dios, y las virtudes del siglo venidero,
texts.heb.6.6: Y han caído en apostasía, ser renovados de nuevo por arrepentimiento, crucificando otra vez para sí mismos al Hijo de Dios, y exponiéndole a vituperio.
texts.heb.6.7: Porque la tierra que embebe la lluvia que muchas veces viene sobre ella, y que engendra yerba oportuna a aquellos por los cuales es labrada, recibe bendición de Dios.
texts.heb.6.8: Mas la que produce espinas y abrojos, es reprobada, y cercana de maldición, y cuyo fin es ser quemada.
texts.heb.6.9: Pero de vosotros, oh amados, confiamos mejores cosas, y más cercanas a salud, aunque hablamos así.
texts.heb.6.10: Porque Dios no es injusto que se olvide de vuestra obra, y del trabajo de amor que habéis mostrado por respeto a su nombre, habiendo ministrado a los santos, y ministrándo los aun.
texts.heb.6.11: Empero deseamos que cada uno de vosotros muestre la misma solicitud hasta el cabo para completa seguridad de su esperanza.
texts.heb.6.12: Que no os hagáis perezosos, mas imitadores de aquellos que por medio de la fe y de la paciencia están heredando las promesas.
texts.heb.6.13: Porque cuando Dios hizo la promesa a Abraham, ya que no podía jurar por otro mayor, juró por sí mismo,
texts.heb.6.14: Diciendo: Ciertamente te bendeciré bendiciendo; y multiplicando, te multiplicaré.
texts.heb.6.15: Y así habiendo esperado con largura de ánimo, alcanzó la promesa.
texts.heb.6.16: Porque los hombres ciertamente por el mayor que ellos juran; y el juramento, para confirmación, es para ellos el término de toda contención.
texts.heb.6.17: En lo cual queriendo Dios mostrar más abundantemente a los herederos de la promesa la inmutabilidad de su consejo, intervino con juramento;
texts.heb.6.18: Para que por dos cosas inmutables, en las cuales era imposible que Dios mintiese, tuviéramos un fortísimo consuelo, los que nos hemos refugiado a trabarnos de la esperanza propuesta;
texts.heb.6.19: La cual tenemos como áncora del alma, tan segura como firme, y que entra hasta del velo adentro:
texts.heb.6.20: Donde entró por nosotros nuestro precursor Jesús, hecho sumo sacerdote por siempre según el orden de Melquisedec.
texts.heb.7.1: Porque este Melquisedec, rey de Salem, sacerdote del Dios Altísimo, el cual salió al encuentro a Abraham que volvía de la matanza de los reyes, y le bendijo:
texts.heb.7.2: A quien asimismo dio Abraham la décima parte de todo: primeramente el cual ciertamente se interpreta, Rey de justicia; y luego también, Rey de Salem, que es, Rey de paz;
texts.heb.7.3: Sin padre, sin madre, sin genealogía; que ni tiene principio de días, ni fin de vida; mas hecho semejante al Hijo de Dios, se queda sacerdote continuamente.
texts.heb.7.4: Considerád pues cuán grande fue éste, a quien aun Abraham el patriarca dio la décima de los despojos.
texts.heb.7.5: Que ciertamente los que de los hijos de Leví reciben el sacerdocio, tienen mandamiento de tomar diezmos del pueblo según la ley, es a saber, de sus hermanos, aunque también ellos hayan salido de los lomos de Abraham.
texts.heb.7.6: Mas aquel, cuya genealogía no es contada entre ellos, tomó diezmos de Abraham, y bendijo al que tenía las promesas.
texts.heb.7.7: Y sin contradicción alguna lo que es menos es bendito de lo que es mejor.
texts.heb.7.8: Y aquí ciertamente los hombres mortales toman los diezmos; mas allí, aquel del cual está dado testimonio, que vive.
texts.heb.7.9: Y (por decirlo así) en Abraham fue diezmado también el mismo Leví que recibe los diezmos;
texts.heb.7.10: Porque aun Leví estaba en los lomos de su padre, cuando Melquisedec salió al encuentro a Abraham.
texts.heb.7.11: Si pues la perfección era por el sacerdocio Levítico, (porque debajo de él recibió el pueblo la ley,) ¿qué necesidad había aun de que se levantase otro sacerdote según el orden de Melquisedec, y que no se dijese según el orden de Aarón?
texts.heb.7.12: Luego traspasado el sacerdocio, necesario es que se haga también traspasamiento de la ley.
texts.heb.7.13: Porque aquel de quien estas cosas se dicen, de otra tribu es, de la cual nadie asistió al altar.
texts.heb.7.14: Porque es evidente que nuestro Señor nació de Judá, de cuya tribu nada habló Moisés, tocante al sacerdocio.
texts.heb.7.15: Y aun mucho más evidente es; que, según la semejanza de Melquisedec, se levanta otro sacerdote:
texts.heb.7.16: El cual no es hecho conforme a la ley del mandamiento carnal, sino según el poder de una vida indisoluble.
texts.heb.7.17: Porque él testifica, diciendo: Tú eres sacerdote para siempre según el orden de Melquisedec.
texts.heb.7.18: El mandamiento precedente cierto se abroga por su flaqueza e inutilidad.
texts.heb.7.19: Porque nada perfeccionó la ley, sino la introducción de mejor esperanza, por la cual nos acercamos de Dios,
texts.heb.7.20: Y tanto más en cuanto no sin juramento fue él hecho sacerdote;
texts.heb.7.21: (Porque los otros cierto sin juramento fueron hechos sacerdotes; mas éste, con juramento por aquel que le dijo: Juró el Señor, y no se arrepentirá: Tú eres sacerdote eternamente según el orden de Melquisedec:)
texts.heb.7.22: Tanto de mejor concierto fue hecho prometedor Jesús.
texts.heb.7.23: Y los otros cierto fueron muchos sacerdotes, porque la muerte les impedía que continuasen;
texts.heb.7.24: Mas éste, porque permanece eternamente, tiene el sacerdocio inmutable.
texts.heb.7.25: Por lo cual puede también salvar perpetuamente a los que por él se allegan a Dios, viviendo siempre para interceder por ellos;
texts.heb.7.26: Porque tal sumo sacerdote nos convenía, que fuese santo, inocente, libre de mancha, apartado de los pecadores, y hecho más sublime que los cielos.
texts.heb.7.27: Que no tuviese necesidad cada día, como los otros sumos sacerdotes, de ofrecer sacrificios, primero por sus propios pecados, y luego por los del pueblo; porque esto lo hizo una vez ofreciéndose a sí mismo.
texts.heb.7.28: Porque la ley constituye sumos sacerdotes a hombres que tienen flaqueza; mas la palabra del juramento, que fue después de la ley, constituye al Hijo, que es perfecto eternamente.
texts.heb.8.1: Así que la suma de las cosas que habemos dicho es esta: Que tenemos tal sumo sacerdote que se asentó a la diestra del trono de la Majestad en los cielos:
texts.heb.8.2: Ministro del santuario, y del verdadero tabernáculo que el Señor asentó, y no hombre.
texts.heb.8.3: Porque todo sumo sacerdote es constituido para ofrecer dones y también sacrificios: por lo cual fue necesario que éste también tuviese algo que ofrecer.
texts.heb.8.4: Porque si él estuviese sobre la tierra, ni aun sería sacerdote, habiendo aun los otros sacerdotes que ofrecen los dones según la ley.
texts.heb.8.5: (Los cuales sirven por bosquejo y sombra de las cosas celestiales, como fue respondido a Moisés cuando había de comenzar a construir el tabernáculo: Mira, pues, dice, haz todas las cosas conforme al dechado que te ha sido mostrado en el monte.)
texts.heb.8.6: Mas ahora él ha alcanzado un ministerio tanto más excelente, cuanto que también él es el mediador de un mejor concierto, el cual ha sido establecido sobre mejores promesas.
texts.heb.8.7: Porque si en aquel primer concierto no hubiera falta, no se hubiera procurado lugar para un segundo.
texts.heb.8.8: Porque reprendiendo los dice: He aquí, vienen días, dice el Señor, y consumaré para con la casa de Israel, y para con la casa de Judá, un nuevo concierto:
texts.heb.8.9: No según el concierto que hice con vuestros padres en el día que los tomé por la mano para sacarlos de la tierra de Egipto; porque ellos no permanecieron en mi concierto, y yo no me cuidé de ellos, dice el Señor.
texts.heb.8.10: Porque éste es el concierto que haré con la casa de Israel después de aquellos días, dice el Señor: Daré mis leyes en la mente de ellos, y sobre el corazón de ellos las escribiré; y yo seré su Dios, y ellos serán mi pueblo:
texts.heb.8.11: Y no enseñará cada uno a su conciudadano, ni cada uno a su hermano, diciendo: Conoce al Señor; porque todos me conocerán desde el menor de ellos hasta el mayor.
texts.heb.8.12: Porque seré propicio a sus injusticias, y a sus pecados; y de sus iniquidades no me acordaré más.
texts.heb.8.13: Diciendo un nuevo concierto, dio por viejo al primero; y lo que es dado por viejo y se envejece, cerca está de desvanecerse.
texts.heb.9.1: Tenía empero por cierto también el primer concierto ordenanzas de culto, y santuario mundano.
texts.heb.9.2: Porque el tabernáculo fue hecho; el primero, en que estaban el candelero, y también la mesa, y los panes de la proposición, el cual es llamado el lugar santo.
texts.heb.9.3: Y detrás del segundo velo estaba el tabernáculo llamado el lugar santísimo,
texts.heb.9.4: Que tenía el incensario de oro, y el arca del concierto cubierta de todas partes al rededor de oro: en que estaba una urna de oro que tenía el maná, y la vara de Aarón que reverdeció, y las tablas del concierto;
texts.heb.9.5: Y sobre ella los querubines de gloria haciendo sombra al propiciatorio: de las cuales cosas no podemos ahora hablar en particular.
texts.heb.9.6: Y estas cosas así ordenadas, en el primer tabernáculo siempre entraban los sacerdotes para cumplir las funciones del culto divino;
texts.heb.9.7: Mas en el segundo, solo el sumo sacerdote entraba una sola vez en el año, no sin sangre, la cual ofrece por sus propios pecados de ignorancia, y por los del pueblo:
texts.heb.9.8: Dando a entender el Espíritu Santo esto, que todavía no estaba patente el camino para el lugar santísimo, entre tanto que el primer tabernáculo estuviese aun en pie.
texts.heb.9.9: Lo cual era figura para aquel tiempo presente, en el cual se ofrecían dones y también sacrificios, que no podían hacer perfecto al que daba culto, en cuanto a la conciencia;
texts.heb.9.10: Que solamente consistía en viandas, y en bebidas, y en diversos lavamientos, y justicias de la carne, impuestas hasta el tiempo de la corrección.
texts.heb.9.11: Mas estando ya presente Cristo, sumo sacerdote de los bienes que han de venir, por medio del mayor y más perfecto tabernáculo, no hecho de manos, es a saber, no de esta creación;
texts.heb.9.12: Ni por la sangre de machos de cabrío, ni de becerros, mas por su propia sangre entró una vez en el santuario, habiendo obtenido redención eterna para nosotros.
texts.heb.9.13: Porque si la sangre de los toros y de los machos de cabrío, y la ceniza de una becerra, rociada sobre los impuros, los santifica para limpiamiento de la carne,
texts.heb.9.14: ¿Cuánto más la sangre de Cristo, el cual por el Espíritu eterno se ofreció a sí mismo sin mancha a Dios, purgará vuestras conciencias de las obras muertas para que deis culto al Dios vivo?
texts.heb.9.15: Y por esta razón él es el mediador del nuevo testamento, para que entreviniendo muerte para la redención de las transgresiones que había debajo del primer testamento, los que son llamados reciban la promesa de la herencia eterna.
texts.heb.9.16: Porque donde hay testamento, necesario es que intervenga la muerte del testador.
texts.heb.9.17: Porque el testamento es firme después de muertos: de otra manera no es válido entre tanto que el testador vive.
texts.heb.9.18: Así que ni aun el primero fue consagrado sin sangre.
texts.heb.9.19: Porque habiendo leído Moisés todos los mandamientos de la ley a todo el pueblo, tomando la sangre de los becerros y de los machos de cabrío, con agua, y lana de grana, e hisopo, asperjó a todo el pueblo, y juntamente al mismo libro,
texts.heb.9.20: Diciendo: Esta es la sangre del testamento que Dios os ha mandado.
texts.heb.9.21: Y allende de esto, el tabernáculo también, y todos los vasos del ministerio asperjó con la sangre.
texts.heb.9.22: Y casi todas las cosas según la ley son purificadas con sangre; y sin derramamiento de sangre no hay remisión.
